children.title: Quadratic-Module Descriptions
children.top_down_role: Certificate systems organized through individual inequality generators.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic closure characterization equivalent to the seed's finitely generated SOS representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A quadratic module \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) satisfies \(1\in Q\), \(Q+Q\subseteq Q\), and \(a^2Q\subseteq Q\) for every \(a\in\mathbb R[x]\). For \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\),
\[
M(g)=\left\{\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i:\sigma_i\in\Sigma[x]\right\}
\]
is the smallest quadratic module containing all \(g_i\). Unlike a preordering, a quadratic module need not be closed under products of arbitrary members.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SOS-weighted generator cone is exactly the smallest quadratic module containing the inequalities, and it need not be multiplicatively closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M(g)=\bigcap\{Q:Q\text{ is a quadratic module and }g_i\in Q\ \forall i\},\qquad M(g)\text{ need not be a preordering}.

notation.meaning: An arbitrary quadratic module of the polynomial ring.

knowledge_statements.title: Generated-Quadratic-Module Minimality

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(g)=\{\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i:\sigma_i\in\Sigma[x]\}\subseteq\{p:p\geq0\text{ on }K(g)\}\).

notation.meaning: Cone of sums-of-squares polynomials in the variables x.
Basic closed set defined by the inequality generators.
Quadratic module generated by the polynomials g_i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard quadratic-module definition from real algebraic geometry; authoritative locator pending
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the finitely generated quadratic module associated with a basic closed semialgebraic set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\) and let \(\Sigma[x]\) denote the sums-of-squares cone. The quadratic module generated by \(g\) is
\[
M(g):=\left\{\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^{m}\sigma_i g_i:\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m\in\Sigma[x]\right\}.
\]
Its elements are nonnegative on \(K(g):=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_i(x)\geq0\text{ for every }i\}\). A certificate of \(f\in M(g)\) consists of the displayed sums-of-squares multipliers and therefore uses each inequality generator only to the first power.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic module consists of sums of squares plus sums-of-squares multiples of individual inequality generators; every represented polynomial is nonnegative on the described set.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Module Descriptions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition, nonnegativity claim, content kind, and local container fit are mathematically standard and internally consistent, but no inspectable authoritative citation with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Preordering Descriptions
children.top_down_role: Certificate systems enlarged by products of defining inequalities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic closure characterization equivalent to the seed's square-free-product representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A preordering \(P\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) contains all squares and is closed under addition and multiplication. For \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\),
\[
T(g)=\left\{\sum_{\alpha\in\{0,1\}^m}\sigma_\alpha g^\alpha:\sigma_\alpha\in\Sigma[x]\right\}
\]
is the smallest preordering containing every \(g_i\). Equivalently, if \(P\) is any preordering with \(g_i\in P\) for all \(i\), then \(T(g)\subseteq P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The square-free-product cone is exactly the smallest multiplicatively closed positivity cone containing the generators and all squares.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T(g)=\bigcap\{P:P\text{ is a preordering and }g_i\in P\ \forall i\}.

notation.meaning: An arbitrary preordering of the polynomial ring.

knowledge_statements.title: Generated-Preordering Minimality

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T(g)=\{\sum_{\alpha\in\{0,1\}^m}\sigma_\alpha g^\alpha:\sigma_\alpha\in\Sigma[x]\}\subseteq\{p:p\geq0\text{ on }K(g)\}\).

notation.meaning: Product of generators selected by the binary multi-index alpha.
Preordering generated by the polynomials g_i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finitely generated preordering definition; authoritative locator pending
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses square-free products because even powers can be absorbed into sums-of-squares multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(\alpha\in\{0,1\}^m\), set \(g^\alpha:=\prod_{i=1}^m g_i^{\alpha_i}\). The preordering generated by \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\) is
\[
T(g):=\left\{\sum_{\alpha\in\{0,1\}^m}\sigma_\alpha g^\alpha:\sigma_\alpha\in\Sigma[x]\right\}.
\]
Every member of \(T(g)\) is nonnegative on \(K(g)\), since every selected generator product and every sums-of-squares multiplier is nonnegative there. Moreover, \(M(g)\subseteq T(g)\), while equality need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A preordering permits sums-of-squares multiples of every square-free product of inequality generators, and therefore contains the corresponding quadratic module.
knowledge_statements.title: Preordering Descriptions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The square-free-product definition and inclusion of the quadratic module are correct and fit the container, but the record has no inspectable authoritative citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Generator Redundancy-Selection Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Dependence of certificate applicability on equivalent, reduced, or augmented descriptions of the same set.

children.title: Minimal Generator Selection
children.top_down_role: Reduced generator families intended to retain certificate-bearing descriptions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary example separating the two meanings of minimal generator selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R\), let \(g_1(x)=x\), \(g_2(x)=-x\), and \(g_3(x)=-x^2\). Both \(\{1,2\}\) and \(\{3\}\) define \(K=\{0\}\). The family \(\{1,2\}\) is inclusion-minimal because deleting either inequality gives a half-line, but it is not minimum-cardinality because \(g_3\geq0\) alone defines \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two opposing linear inequalities form an inclusion-minimal description of zero, although one quadratic inequality gives a smaller description.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K_{\{1,2\}}=K_{\{3\}}=\{0\},\qquad \{1,2\}\text{ is inclusion-minimal but not cardinality-minimum}.
knowledge_statements.title: Inclusion-Minimal Need Not Be Cardinality-Minimum

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the alternative meaning of minimal and distinguishes it from the seed's inclusion-minimal interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(K_J:=\{x:g_j(x)\geq0\text{ for all }j\in J\}\), a minimum-cardinality selection is
\[
J_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{|J|:J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\},\ K_J=K\}.
\]
Every minimum-cardinality selection is inclusion-minimal, but the converse can fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimum-cardinality selection uses as few original inequalities as possible; it is inclusion-minimal, but an inclusion-minimal selection need not be smallest.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: J_*\in\arg\min\{|J|:K_J=K\}\Longrightarrow J_*\text{ is inclusion-minimal}.

notation.meaning: Minimum-cardinality index set preserving the feasible set.

review_flags: terminology_boundary: minimum cardinality is stronger than inclusion-minimality
knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Cardinality Generator Selection

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) is inclusion-minimal exactly when \(K_J=K\) and \(K_{J\setminus\{j\}}\neq K\) for every \(j\in J\).

notation.meaning: Set described by the generators indexed by J.
An inclusion-minimal index set describing K.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: inclusion-minimal generator selection is a standard irredundancy condition
terminology_ambiguity: minimal may alternatively mean minimum cardinality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interprets minimal as inclusion-minimal, not necessarily minimum-cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), define \(K_J:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_j(x)\geq0\text{ for all }j\in J\}\). The subfamily indexed by \(J\) is an inclusion-minimal generator selection for \(K\) precisely when
\[
K_J=K\quad\text{and}\quad K_{J\setminus\{j\}}\neq K\quad\text{for every }j\in J.
\]
Thus every selected inequality is necessary for this particular set description. This condition concerns equality of feasible sets and does not assert that the associated quadratic module or preordering is minimal or unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generator subfamily is inclusion-minimal when it defines the same feasible set but deleting any one selected inequality enlarges that set.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Generator Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated condition correctly characterizes inclusion-minimality, and the scope note distinguishes it from minimum cardinality. A source is still required to support this selected interpretation of the terminal title.

children.title: Redundant Generator Effects
children.top_down_role: Certificate consequences of retaining logically unnecessary inequalities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic effect of a set-redundant generator on the Archimedean property of its quadratic module.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(r\geq0\) on \(K(g)\), then \(K(g,r)=K(g)\) and \(M(g)\subseteq M(g,r)\). Hence
\[
M(g)\text{ Archimedean}\Longrightarrow M(g,r)\text{ Archimedean}.
\]
The converse can fail: a valid redundant bounding polynomial can provide a ball certificate absent from the original module.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a valid redundant inequality cannot destroy Archimedeanity and can create it by supplying a missing algebraic bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M(g)\text{ Archimedean}\Longrightarrow M(g,r)\text{ Archimedean},\qquad\text{while the converse can fail}.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Archimedeanity is preserved under inclusion of quadratic modules
knowledge_statements.title: Archimedeanity under Redundant Augmentation

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K(g,r)=K(g)\), \(M(g)\subseteq M(g,r)\), and \(T(g)\subseteq T(g,r)\).

notation.meaning: Quadratic module after adjoining r as an inequality generator.
Preordering after adjoining r as an inequality generator.
Feasible set after adjoining the inequality r >= 0.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: follows directly from standard generated-cone definitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates feasible-set redundancy from redundancy inside a certificate cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(r\) is nonnegative on \(K(g)\), and adjoin \(r\geq0\) to the description. Then \(K(g,r)=K(g)\), but the generated certificate cones satisfy
\[
M(g)\subseteq M(g,r),\qquad T(g)\subseteq T(g,r).
\]
Either inclusion may be strict even though the feasible set is unchanged. If \(r\in M(g)\), then \(M(g,r)=M(g)\); if \(r\in T(g)\), then \(T(g,r)=T(g)\). At fixed degree, adjoining \(r\) can nevertheless change available representations and relaxation strength through its degree and multiplier bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set-redundant inequality can enlarge certificate cones and strengthen finite-degree relaxations; cone membership of the new generator ensures no untruncated enlargement.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Generator Effects

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasible-set equality, cone inclusions, and cone-membership equality conditions are correct and fit the property container. The strict-inclusion and finite-degree sensitivity claims require an inspectable source.

children.title: Equivalent Description Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Variation in certificate applicability across descriptions of the same feasible set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: An exact invariance class within the broader presentation-sensitive setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c_1,\ldots,c_m>0\) and \(\tilde g_i=c_i g_i\). Then
\[
K(\tilde g)=K(g),\qquad M(\tilde g)=M(g),\qquad T(\tilde g)=T(g).
\]
For total-degree truncations, \(M_d(\tilde g)=M_d(g)\) and \(T_d(\tilde g)=T_d(g)\) for every \(d\), since positive constants can be absorbed into SOS multipliers without changing degrees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive constant rescaling of individual inequalities preserves the feasible set, full certificate cones, and standard total-degree truncations.
assumptions_latex: Truncations bound the total degree of each weighted term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K(c_1g_1,\ldots,c_mg_m)=K(g),\quad M(cg)=M(g),\quad T(cg)=T(g),\quad M_d(cg)=M_d(g),\quad T_d(cg)=T_d(g).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive constants are absorbed into SOS multipliers without changing total degree
knowledge_statements.title: Positive Generator-Scaling Invariance

assumptions_latex: \(K(g)=K(\tilde g)\) for two finite polynomial inequality descriptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K(g)=K(\tilde g)\) does not imply \(M(g)=M(\tilde g)\), \(T(g)=T(\tilde g)\), or equality of their degree truncations.

notation.meaning: Quadratic modules generated by the respective descriptions.
Preorderings generated by the respective descriptions.
Degree-2d truncation of the corresponding certificate cone.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: presentation dependence of generated certificate cones is standard
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-set equivalence alone does not identify algebraic certificate systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Equality of basic closed sets,
\[
K(g)=K(\tilde g),
\]
does not in general imply \(M(g)=M(\tilde g)\) or \(T(g)=T(\tilde g)\). It also does not imply equality of degree-truncated cones \(M_d(g)=M_d(\tilde g)\) or \(T_d(g)=T_d(\tilde g)\). Hence certificate existence at a prescribed degree, relaxation values, and Archimedean properties may depend on the chosen generators rather than only on the underlying semialgebraic set. Equality of the relevant generated cones is an additional algebraic requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two generator lists may define the same feasible set while producing different certificate cones, truncations, relaxation values, or Archimedean behavior.
knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent Description Sensitivity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure boundary appropriately distinguishes set equivalence from equality of generated and truncated certificate cones. Its claims about relaxation values and Archimedean behavior need authoritative source support.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sphere scalarization of a universally quantified polynomial matrix inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fiberwise equivalence between negative semidefiniteness and scalar quadratic-form inequalities over a unit-sphere variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbf K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^p\), \(\mathbf B\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let \(\mathbf F(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\in\mathcal S_m\) be a symmetric polynomial matrix. Define
\[
\mathbf Z=\{\mathbf z\in\mathbb R^m:\|\mathbf z\|=1\},\qquad \widehat{\mathbf K}=\mathbf K\times\mathbf Z,
\]
and \(f(\mathbf x,\mathbf y,\mathbf z)=\mathbf z^T\mathbf F(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\mathbf z\). Then
\[
\{\mathbf x\in\mathbf B:\mathbf F(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\preceq0\ \forall\mathbf y\in\mathbf K_{\mathbf x}\}
=
\{\mathbf x\in\mathbf B:f(\mathbf x,\mathbf y,\mathbf z)\leq0\ \forall(\mathbf y,\mathbf z)\in\widehat{\mathbf K}_{\mathbf x}\}.
\]
The quantified polynomial methodology cited in the source applies to this scalar representation despite the unit-sphere factor having empty interior in its ambient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric polynomial matrix is negative semidefinite for every admissible uncertainty value exactly when every associated quadratic form is nonpositive for every admissible uncertainty value and every unit vector. The sphere-constrained scalar formulation is still covered by the cited quantified approximation methodology.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf F(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\in\mathcal S_m\text{ is a symmetric polynomial matrix}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf F(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\preceq0\ \forall\mathbf y\in\mathbf K_{\mathbf x}\iff \mathbf z^T\mathbf F(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\mathbf z\leq0\ \forall(\mathbf y,\mathbf z)\in\widehat{\mathbf K}_{\mathbf x}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sphere scalarization and conditional volume approximation of a polynomial matrix inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scalarization and conditional convergence; the source's automatic zero-level-set claim for every nontrivial matrix polynomial is not retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbf B\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a box and let \(\mathbf A(\mathbf x)\in\mathcal S_m\) be a symmetric polynomial matrix. With
\[
\mathbf Y=\{\mathbf y\in\mathbb R^m:\|\mathbf y\|^2=1\},\qquad f(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)=-\mathbf y^T\mathbf A(\mathbf x)\mathbf y,
\]
one has
\[
\mathbf S:=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbf B:\mathbf A(\mathbf x)\succeq0\}
=
\{\mathbf x\in\mathbf B:f(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\leq0\ \forall\mathbf y\in\mathbf Y\}.
\]
The quantified polynomial hierarchy described in the source produces inner approximations \(\mathbf R_f^k=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbf B:p_k(\mathbf x)\leq0\}\subseteq\mathbf S\). If
\[
\{\mathbf x\in\mathbf B:\lambda_{\max}(-\mathbf A(\mathbf x))=0\}
\]
has Lebesgue measure zero, then \(\operatorname{vol}(\mathbf R_f^k)\to\operatorname{vol}(\mathbf S)\). If every entry of \(\mathbf A\) has degree at most \(d\), then \(\deg f\leq d+2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive semidefiniteness of a symmetric polynomial matrix is equivalent to nonpositivity of its negated quadratic form for every unit vector. This yields polynomial inner approximations with volume convergence when the zero level set of the maximal eigenvalue has measure zero; the scalarized polynomial has degree at most d+2.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf A(\mathbf x)\in\mathcal S_m\text{ is a polynomial matrix}
\operatorname{vol}\{\mathbf x\in\mathbf B:\lambda_{\max}(-\mathbf A(\mathbf x))=0\}=0\text{ for volume convergence}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf S=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbf B:-\mathbf y^T\mathbf A(\mathbf x)\mathbf y\leq0\ \forall\mathbf y\in\mathbf Y\},\quad \mathbf R_f^k\subseteq\mathbf S,\quad \operatorname{vol}(\mathbf R_f^k)\to\operatorname{vol}(\mathbf S)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inner approximation and certification of semialgebraic fiber containment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiple polynomial inequalities are approximated separately and intersected; volume convergence requires a measure-zero active boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbf F=\{(\mathbf x,\mathbf y):\mathbf x\in\mathbf B,\ f_\ell(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\le0,\ \ell=1,\ldots,q\}\) and \[\mathbf R_{\mathbf F}=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbf B:\mathbf K_{\mathbf x}\subseteq\mathbf F_{\mathbf x}\}.\] For each \(\ell\), let \(p_{k\ell}\) be a polynomial upper approximation of \(\overline J_{f_\ell}(\mathbf x)=\sup_{\mathbf y\in\mathbf K_{\mathbf x}}f_\ell(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\), and define \[\mathbf R_{\mathbf F}^k=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbf B:p_{k\ell}(\mathbf x)\le0,\ \ell=1,\ldots,q\}=\bigcap_{\ell=1}^q\mathbf R_{f_\ell}^k.\] Then \(\mathbf R_{\mathbf F}^k\subseteq\mathbf R_{\mathbf F}\). If \[\{\mathbf x\in\mathbf B:\sup_{\mathbf y\in\mathbf K_{\mathbf x}}\max_{1\le\ell\le q}f_\ell(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)=0\}\] has Lebesgue measure zero, then \(\operatorname{vol}(\mathbf R_{\mathbf F}^k)\to\operatorname{vol}(\mathbf R_{\mathbf F})\). Moreover, \(\mathbf K\subseteq\mathbf F\) iff \(\mathbf R_{\mathbf F}=\mathbf B\), and the finite condition \(\mathbf R_{\mathbf F}^k=\mathbf B\) for some \(k\) is sufficient to certify this containment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a target fiber defined by finitely many polynomial inequalities, intersecting the separate polynomial inner approximations gives an inner approximation of the parameter values whose source fiber is contained in the target fiber. Its volume converges under a measure-zero boundary condition. Global containment is equivalent to the exact parameter set being the whole box, and equality of a finite inner approximation with the box is a sufficient containment certificate.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf F=\{(\mathbf x,\mathbf y):\mathbf x\in\mathbf B,\ f_\ell(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\le0,\ \ell=1,\ldots,q\}
\overline J_{f_\ell}(\mathbf x)=\sup_{\mathbf y\in\mathbf K_{\mathbf x}}f_\ell(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)
\operatorname{vol}\{\mathbf x\in\mathbf B:\sup_{\mathbf y\in\mathbf K_{\mathbf x}}\max_\ell f_\ell(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)=0\}=0\text{ for volume convergence}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf R_{\mathbf F}^k=\bigcap_{\ell=1}^q\mathbf R_{f_\ell}^k\subseteq\mathbf R_{\mathbf F},\quad \operatorname{vol}(\mathbf R_{\mathbf F}^k)\to\operatorname{vol}(\mathbf R_{\mathbf F}),\quad \mathbf R_{\mathbf F}^k=\mathbf B\Rightarrow\mathbf K\subseteq\mathbf F

children.title: Augmented Generator Systems
children.top_down_role: Description families enriched with additional valid inequalities.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K(g,r)=K(g)\), \(M(g)\subseteq M(g,r)\), and \(T(g)\subseteq T(g,r)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard augmentation of a semialgebraic generator system
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Augmentation adds valid inequalities while preserving the represented feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An augmented generator system is a concatenated family \((g,r)=(g_1,\ldots,g_m,r_1,\ldots,r_s)\) in which each added polynomial \(r_j\) is nonnegative on \(K(g)\). It defines
\[
K(g,r):=\{x:g_i(x)\geq0\text{ for all }i, r_j(x)\geq0\text{ for all }j\}=K(g).
\]
The associated cones contain the original ones: \(M(g)\subseteq M(g,r)\) and \(T(g)\subseteq T(g,r)\). The augmentation is certificate-redundant only when the corresponding generated cone remains equal to the original cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An augmented system adds inequalities valid on the original feasible set, preserving that set while potentially enlarging its algebraic certificate cones.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmented Generator Systems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and stated set and cone relations are correct and fit the augmented-system container, but no inspectable authoritative citation is supplied.

children.title: Generated-Ideal Representation
children.top_down_role: Equality information retained through the ideal generated by the supplied equations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that full-ideal invariance does not imply identical finite-order certificate spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(\mathbb R[x]\), the lists \(h=(x)\) and \(g=(x+x^2,x^2)\) generate the same ideal because \(x=(x+x^2)-x^2\). For the termwise truncation \(I_{\le1}(u)=\{\sum_iq_iu_i:\deg(q_iu_i)\le1\}\), however, \(x\in I_{\le1}(h)\) while \(I_{\le1}(g)=\{0\}\). Thus equivalent generators can yield different truncated certificate spaces and different first relaxation orders.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent equality generators can produce different degree-truncated ideal certificate spaces.
assumptions_latex: Truncation is imposed termwise by \(\deg(q_iu_i)\le D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I(h)=I(g)\text{ does not imply }I_{\le D}(h)=I_{\le D}(g).

notation.meaning: degree-D termwise-truncated multiplier span of u

knowledge_statements.title: Generator Dependence of Degree Truncations

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generator Invariance of the Full Ideal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when two supplied equality lists retain identical untruncated algebraic consequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite polynomial lists \(h=(h_1,\ldots,h_r)\) and \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_s)\), define \(I(h)=\{\sum_iq_ih_i:q_i\in\mathbb R[x]\}\). Then \(I(h)=I(g)\) if and only if every \(h_i\) belongs to \(I(g)\) and every \(g_j\) belongs to \(I(h)\). Consequently the two lists have identical untruncated ideal-membership consequences and identical quotient rings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two equality lists generate the same ideal exactly when each list is polynomially derivable from the other.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I(h)=I(g)\iff(h_i\in I(g)\ \forall i\text{ and }g_j\in I(h)\ \forall j).

notation.meaning: ideal generated by the equality list h

knowledge_statements.title: Generator Invariance of the Full Ideal

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I(h)=\{\sum_{j=1}^r q_jh_j:q_j\in\mathbb{R}[x]\}\), and every member vanishes on \(V_{\mathbb R}(h)\).

notation.meaning: Ideal generated by the equality polynomials.
Common real zero set of the equality generators.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retains exactly the polynomial consequences generated algebraically by the supplied equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For equality generators \(h=(h_1,\ldots,h_r)\), their generated ideal is
\[
I(h):=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_r\rangle=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^{r}q_jh_j:q_j\in\mathbb{R}[x]\right\}.
\]
Every \(p\in I(h)\) vanishes on \(V_{\mathbb R}(h):=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:h_j(x)=0\text{ for all }j\}\). Thus an ideal certificate for an equality consequence \(p=0\) is the explicit multiplier tuple \((q_1,\ldots,q_r)\). The reverse inclusion in the full real vanishing ideal need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The generated ideal contains all polynomial combinations of the supplied equations; each such combination vanishes on their common real solution set.
knowledge_statements.title: Generated-Ideal Representation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generated-ideal representation and vanishing implication are correct and properly distinguished from the full real vanishing ideal, but the record lacks an inspectable citation.

children.title: Quotient-Ring Representation
children.top_down_role: Equality relations absorbed into the ambient coordinate algebra.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes maps from the generated-ideal quotient without replacing that ideal by the real vanishing ideal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R=\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), \(I\triangleleft R\), and \(\pi:R\to R/I\). Every \(\mathbb R\)-algebra homomorphism \(\varphi:R\to B\) with \(I\subseteq\ker\varphi\) factors uniquely as \(\varphi=\bar\varphi\circ\pi\). Consequently, evaluation gives a bijection \(V_{\mathbb R}(I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R\text{-alg}}(R/I,\mathbb R)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maps annihilating the equality ideal factor uniquely through the quotient, whose real-valued algebra homomorphisms are precisely evaluations at real zeros of the ideal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I\subseteq\ker\varphi\Longrightarrow\exists!\,\bar\varphi:R/I\to B\text{ with }\varphi=\bar\varphi\circ\pi;\qquad V_{\mathbb R}(I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R\text{-alg}}(R/I,\mathbb R).

notation.meaning: Common real zero set of the ideal.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: universal property of quotient rings and evaluation correspondence
knowledge_statements.title: Universal Property and Real-Point Correspondence

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([p]=[q]\text{ in }\mathbb{R}[x]/I\iff p-q\in I\), and \([h_j]=[0]\) for every \(j\).

notation.meaning: Quotient coordinate algebra modulo the equality ideal.
Residue class of a polynomial p modulo I.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absorbs generated equality relations, not automatically every polynomial vanishing on the real solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_r\rangle\). The equality-constrained coordinate algebra is the quotient
\[
A:=\mathbb{R}[x]/I.
\]
For \(p,q\in\mathbb{R}[x]\), their residue classes satisfy \([p]=[q]\) in \(A\) exactly when \(p-q\in I\). In particular, \([h_j]=[0]\) for every equality generator. Polynomial objectives and inequality generators may therefore be replaced by their residue classes, with addition and multiplication induced from \(\mathbb{R}[x]\). If \(I\) is smaller than the real vanishing ideal, the quotient retains nonzero classes that vanish at every real feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quotienting by the generated ideal makes each supplied equation algebraically zero and identifies polynomials whose difference belongs to that ideal.
knowledge_statements.title: Quotient-Ring Representation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quotient-ring representation is mathematically correct, fully quantified, and suited to the terminal container. No authoritative source with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Real Vanishing-Ideal Representation
children.top_down_role: Equality information completed by all polynomial relations on the real solution set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the algebraic membership characterization of all relations visible on the real zero set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an ideal \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\),
\[
\sqrt[\mathbb R]{I}=\left\{p:\exists m\geq1,\ \exists q_1,\ldots,q_s\in\mathbb R[x],\quad p^{2m}+\sum_{j=1}^s q_j^2\in I\right\}.
\]
By the Real Nullstellensatz, \(p\) vanishes on \(V_{\mathbb R}(I)\) if and only if it satisfies such an identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial vanishes on the real zero set exactly when an even power of it plus a sum of squares belongs to the original ideal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\in I(V_{\mathbb R}(I))=\sqrt[\mathbb R]{I}\iff\exists m\geq1,\ q_1,\ldots,q_s:\ p^{2m}+\sum_jq_j^2\in I.

notation.meaning: Real radical of the ideal I.

knowledge_statements.title: Real-Radical Membership Criterion

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I(V_{\mathbb R}(h))=\{p:p(x)=0\text{ for all }x\in V_{\mathbb R}(h)\}=\sqrt[\mathbb R]{I(h)}\).

notation.meaning: Ideal of all polynomials vanishing on a real set V.
Real radical of the generated ideal.
Common real zero set of the equality generators.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: real vanishing ideal and Real Nullstellensatz identity are standard
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the real, rather than complex, vanishing ideal of the equality set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The real vanishing ideal of the equality set is
\[
I(V_{\mathbb R}(h)):=\{p\in\mathbb{R}[x]:p(x)=0\text{ for every }x\in V_{\mathbb R}(h)\}.
\]
It contains \(I(h)=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_r\rangle\) and, by the Real Nullstellensatz, satisfies \(I(V_{\mathbb R}(h))=\sqrt[\mathbb R]{I(h)}\). Thus this representation records every polynomial equality valid on the real solution set, including consequences not expressible as ordinary ideal combinations of the supplied generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The real vanishing ideal contains exactly all polynomials zero on the real equality set and equals the real radical of the generated ideal.
knowledge_statements.title: Real Vanishing-Ideal Representation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is correct, but the Real Nullstellensatz identity is a substantive theorem and requires an inspectable authoritative citation with a precise locator.

children.title: Mixed Equality-Inequality Systems
children.top_down_role: Certificate containers combining equality ideals with inequality positivity structures.

children.title: Ideal-plus-Quadratic-Module Systems
children.top_down_role: Mixed descriptions pairing an equality ideal with a quadratic module.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quotient-Algebra Representation of the Mixed Quadratic Module
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic formulation of equality-augmented quadratic-module certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=I(h)\), \(A=\mathbb R[x]/I\), and \(\pi:\mathbb R[x]\to A\). If \(M_A(\pi(g))\) is the quadratic module generated by the residue classes of the inequalities, then \[I+M(g)=\pi^{-1}(M_A(\pi(g))),\qquad (I+M(g))/I=M_A(\pi(g)).\] Moreover, the mixed cone is Archimedean exactly when some \(R>0\) satisfies \(R-\sum_i x_i^2\in I+M(g)\), equivalently when the corresponding residue class belongs to \(M_A(\pi(g))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ideal-plus-quadratic-module system is a quadratic module in the equality quotient, where its Archimedean ball condition can also be stated.

notation.meaning: Quadratic module generated in the quotient algebra.
Canonical quotient map modulo the equality ideal.

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient-Algebra Representation of the Mixed Quadratic Module
Ideal-plus-Quadratic-Module Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed certificates use unrestricted equality multipliers and sums-of-squares inequality multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(K(h,g):=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:h_j(x)=0\text{ for all }j,\ g_i(x)\geq0\text{ for all }i\}\), the ideal-plus-quadratic-module cone is
\[
I(h)+M(g)=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^{r}q_jh_j+\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^{m}\sigma_i g_i:q_j\in\mathbb{R}[x],\ \sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m\in\Sigma[x]\right\}.
\]
Membership of \(p\) in this cone certifies \(p(x)\geq0\) for every \(x\in K(h,g)\), because the ideal term vanishes and the remaining terms are nonnegative there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial is certified nonnegative by expressing it as an equality-ideal combination plus a quadratic-module expression in the inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I(h)+M(g)\subseteq\{p\in\mathbb{R}[x]:p(x)\geq0\text{ for every }x\in K(h,g)\}\).

notation.meaning: Ideal generated by the equality polynomials.
Quadratic module generated by the inequality polynomials.
Cone of sums-of-squares polynomials in the variables x.

children.title: Ideal-plus-Preordering Systems
children.top_down_role: Mixed descriptions pairing an equality ideal with a preordering.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact emptiness certificate for polynomial equalities and weak inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K(h,g)=\{x:h_j(x)=0,\ g_i(x)\ge0\}\), \[K(h,g)=\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad -1\in I(h)+T(g).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed equality and weak-inequality system is infeasible exactly when minus one has an ideal-plus-preordering representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K(h,g)=\varnothing\iff -1\in I(h)+T(g).

notation.meaning: Preordering generated by the weak inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Preordering Infeasibility Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quotient-Algebra Representation of the Mixed Preordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic formulation of the preordering modulo equality relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=I(h)\), \(A=\mathbb R[x]/I\), and \(\pi:\mathbb R[x]\to A\). If \(T_A(\pi(g))\) is the preordering generated by the residue classes of the inequalities, then \[I+T(g)=\pi^{-1}(T_A(\pi(g))),\qquad (I+T(g))/I=T_A(\pi(g)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mixed cone is precisely the inverse image of the inequality preordering in the quotient by the equality ideal.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi:\mathbb R[x]\to\mathbb R[x]/I\) is the quotient map.

notation.meaning: Quotient algebra imposing the equality relations.
Preordering generated in the quotient algebra.

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient-Algebra Representation of the Mixed Preordering

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact strict-positivity theorem for a preordering modulo equality relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K(h,g)=\{x:h_j(x)=0,\ g_i(x)\ge0\}\) is compact and \(p>0\) on \(K(h,g)\), then \[p\in I(h)+T(g).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict positivity on a compact mixed feasible set has an ideal-plus-preordering certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\in I(h)+T(g).

notation.meaning: Preordering generated by the inequality polynomials.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Schmüdgen Strict-Positivity Certificate

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I(h)+T(g)\subseteq\{p:p\geq0\text{ on }K(h,g)\}\).

notation.meaning: Ideal generated by the equality polynomials.
Preordering generated by the inequality polynomials.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The inequality component permits every square-free product of defining inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the mixed feasible set \(K(h,g)\), the ideal-plus-preordering cone is
\[
I(h)+T(g)=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^{r}q_jh_j+\sum_{\alpha\in\{0,1\}^m}\sigma_\alpha g^\alpha:q_j\in\mathbb{R}[x], \sigma_\alpha\in\Sigma[x]\right\}.
\]
Any displayed representation of \(p\) certifies \(p(x)\geq0\) on \(K(h,g)\): the equality-ideal component vanishes there, and every preordering summand is nonnegative. Since \(M(g)\subseteq T(g)\), one has \(I(h)+M(g)\subseteq I(h)+T(g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This certificate adds an equality-ideal combination to sums-of-squares multiples of all square-free products of inequality generators.
knowledge_statements.title: Ideal-plus-Preordering Systems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mixed certificate, quantification, and certificate content kind are correct and fit the terminal container, but no inspectable authoritative citation is supplied.

children.title: Equality-Encoding Variants
children.top_down_role: Alternative encodings whose ideal, certificate, and truncation behavior differ.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariance of the full equality-augmented cone versus presentation-dependent truncations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(I(h)=I(\widetilde h)\), then for every fixed inequality certificate cone \(C\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\), \[I(h)+C=I(\widetilde h)+C.\] Generator-wise finite-degree truncations need not coincide, because converting between the two generating lists may increase multiplier degrees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality lists generating the same ideal give the same full certificate cone, although their natural generator-based truncations can differ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I(h)+C=I(\widetilde h)+C.

notation.meaning: Ideal generated by the entries of h.

knowledge_statements.title: Ideal-Preserving Changes of Equality Generators

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-equivalent conversion of equalities and its effect on the full quadratic module.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(h=(h_1,\ldots,h_r)\) and inequalities \(g\), \[\{h=0,\ g\ge0\}=\{h\ge0,-h\ge0,\ g\ge0\},\qquad M(g,h,-h)=I(h)+M(g).\] The cone identity is untruncated; the natural finite-degree truncations can differ because expressing an arbitrary equality multiplier as a difference of sums of squares may increase degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two opposite weak inequalities preserve the feasible set and full quadratic-module cone of an equality, but need not preserve finite truncations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M(g,h,-h)=I(h)+M(g).

notation.meaning: Quadratic module generated by the listed inequalities.
Ideal generated by the equality polynomials.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality as Two Opposite Inequalities
Equality-Encoding Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-equivalent equality encodings need not be ideal-equivalent or truncation-equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any nonconstant polynomial \(h\in\mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), the equations \(h=0\) and \(h^3=0\) have the same real solution set:
\[
V_{\mathbb R}(h)=V_{\mathbb R}(h^3).
\]
Nevertheless, \(\langle h^3\rangle\subsetneq\langle h\rangle\), so \(\mathbb{R}[x]/\langle h^3\rangle\) and \(\mathbb{R}[x]/\langle h\rangle\) impose different algebraic relations. Consequently, replacing equality generators by set-equivalent ones can change ideal-based certificates and their degree truncations, even though the real feasible set and its real vanishing ideal are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonconstant polynomial h, the equations h=0 and h cubed=0 define the same real set but different generated ideals, quotient algebras, and potentially different finite-degree certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_{\mathbb R}(h)=V_{\mathbb R}(h^3)\) but \(\langle h^3\rangle\subsetneq\langle h\rangle\), so the quotient algebras differ and ideal-based degree truncations can differ.

notation.meaning: Principal ideal generated by a polynomial p.
Real zero set of a polynomial p.

children.title: Running-Intersection Regime
children.top_down_role: Clique-overlap structure supporting globally coherent sparse certificate systems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-free equivalent formulation of the running-intersection regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite family of blocks \(I_1,\ldots,I_m\) admits a running-intersection ordering if and only if there exists a tree on the blocks such that, for every variable index \(i\), the set \(\{k:i\in I_k\}\) induces a connected subtree. Such a tree is a join tree or clique tree; rooting it and listing every parent before its children recovers a running-intersection ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Running intersection is equivalent to a join tree in which all blocks containing any fixed variable form a connected subtree.
assumptions_latex: \(I_1,\ldots,I_m\) is a finite family of nonempty sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A running-intersection ordering exists}\iff\text{a join tree with the connected-subtree property exists}.
knowledge_statements.title: Join-Tree Characterization of Running Intersection

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ordered family satisfies the running-intersection condition precisely when, for every \(k=2,\ldots,m\), there exists \(p(k)<k\) such that \[I_k\cap\bigcup_{j<k}I_j\subseteq I_{p(k)}.\]

notation.meaning: Variable block, also called a clique.
A preceding block containing the separator of block \(k\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite ordered variable blocks in correlative-sparsity decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_1,\ldots,I_m\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be nonempty variable-index blocks. They are in the running-intersection regime if they admit an ordering such that, for each \(k>1\), some earlier block contains every variable shared by \(I_k\) and the preceding blocks: \[I_k\cap\bigcup_{j<k}I_j\subseteq I_{p(k)}\quad\text{for some }p(k)<k.\] The set on the left is the separator through which block \(I_k\) attaches to the preceding blocks. This condition is the clique-tree compatibility assumption used when assembling block-supported polynomial or moment certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ordered block family has running intersection when each new block's overlap with all preceding blocks is contained in one preceding block.
knowledge_statements.title: Running-Intersection Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is mathematically standard and the content kind fits the leaf, but no source supports the stated sparse polynomial/moment-certificate context.

children.title: Clique-Wise Archimedeanity
children.top_down_role: Local boundedness conditions aligned with the blocks of a sparse description.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Boundedness from Clique-Wise Ball Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric consequence of local Archimedeanity when the blocks cover all global variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\bigcup_{k=1}^m I_k=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and, for every block, \(R_k-\sum_{i\in I_k}x_i^2\in I(h^{(k)})+Q(g^{(k)})\). Every point satisfying all assigned local constraints obeys \[\|x\|_2^2\le \sum_{k=1}^m\sum_{i\in I_k}x_i^2\le\sum_{k=1}^mR_k.\] Hence the global feasible set is compact. Running intersection is not needed for this boundedness implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clique-wise ball certificates on blocks covering every variable imply global compactness independently of running intersection.
assumptions_latex: Each local equality-augmented module contains the displayed block ball polynomial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\subseteq\{x:\|x\|_2^2\le\sum_kR_k\},\text{ hence }K\text{ is compact}.

notation.meaning: Feasible set satisfying all locally assigned constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Boundedness from Clique-Wise Ball Certificates

assumptions_latex: For each block \(I_k\), let \(h^{(k)}\) and \(g^{(k)}\) be local equality and inequality polynomials in \(\mathbb R[x_{I_k}]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Clique-wise Archimedeanity holds when, for every \(k\), there is \(R_k>0\) satisfying \[R_k-\sum_{i\in I_k}x_i^2\in I(h^{(k)})+Q(g^{(k)}).\]

notation.meaning: Ideal generated by the local equalities.
Quadratic module generated by the local inequalities.
Polynomial ring on variables indexed by \(I_k\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise quadratic modules augmented by local equality ideals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each variable block \(I_k\), form the local certificate cone \(M_k=I(h^{(k)})+Q(g^{(k)})\subseteq\mathbb R[x_{I_k}]\). The sparse description is clique-wise Archimedean if, for every \(k\), there exists \(R_k>0\) such that \[R_k-\sum_{i\in I_k}x_i^2\in M_k.\] Consequently, every point satisfying the constraints assigned to block \(I_k\) lies in the corresponding closed ball. The condition is local to the chosen blocks and generators; obtaining a global sparse certificate additionally requires an appropriate overlap regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each block is Archimedean when its local equality-augmented quadratic module contains a ball polynomial involving all variables of that block.
knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Wise Archimedeanity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The blockwise ball-membership condition is precise and appropriately classified, but the equality-augmented local-module convention and its sparse-certificate scope require a source.

children.title: Local Equality-Ideal Consistency
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of equality relations across overlapping sparse blocks.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional sufficient witness for agreement of local ideal contractions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J_k\subseteq\mathbb R[x_{I_k}]\). If an ideal \(J\subseteq\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) satisfies \[J_k=J\cap\mathbb R[x_{I_k}]\quad\text{for every }k,\] then, for every pair \(k,\ell\), \[J_k\cap\mathbb R[x_{I_k\cap I_\ell}]=J_\ell\cap\mathbb R[x_{I_k\cap I_\ell}].\] This sufficient condition does not make pairwise contraction agreement sufficient for a global extension or a common real solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contractions of one global ideal necessarily agree on every overlap, but pairwise agreement need not produce a global ideal or common real solution.
assumptions_latex: There exists \(J\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) with \(J_k=J\cap\mathbb R[x_{I_k}]\) for every k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: J_k\cap\mathbb R[x_{I_k\cap I_\ell}]=J_\ell\cap\mathbb R[x_{I_k\cap I_\ell}]\quad\forall k,\ell.

notation.meaning: Global ideal whose contractions are the local ideals.
Variable overlap of blocks k and ell.

knowledge_statements.title: Global-Ideal Extension Witness

assumptions_latex: Let \(J_k\subseteq\mathbb R[x_{I_k}]\) be the ideal generated by the equalities assigned to block \(I_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local equality-ideal consistency means that for every adjacent pair \(k,\ell\), with \(S_{k\ell}=I_k\cap I_\ell\), \[J_k\cap\mathbb R[x_{S_{k\ell}}]=J_\ell\cap\mathbb R[x_{S_{k\ell}}].\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contraction consistency on overlaps of adjacent sparse blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J_k\subseteq\mathbb R[x_{I_k}]\) be the ideal generated by the equality constraints assigned to block \(I_k\). For each adjacent pair of blocks, put \(S_{k\ell}=I_k\cap I_\ell\). The local equality ideals are overlap-consistent when their contractions to the common polynomial ring agree: \[J_k\cap\mathbb R[x_{S_{k\ell}}]=J_\ell\cap\mathbb R[x_{S_{k\ell}}].\] Thus both blocks impose the same polynomial consequences involving only their shared variables. This is a local compatibility condition and, without an acyclic overlap structure or a global extension condition, does not alone guarantee joint consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local equality ideals are consistent when they induce exactly the same polynomial relations on every adjacent block overlap.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Equality-Ideal Consistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed contraction-equality condition is coherent, but adjacency is not defined and no source establishes that this is the intended equality-ideal compatibility notion for the leaf.

children.title: Sparse-Decomposition Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Overlap and support patterns for which local certificates need not assemble into a global certificate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by a polynomial interaction supported in no local block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(I_1=\{1,2\}\) and \(I_2=\{2,3\}\), \[x_1x_3\notin\mathbb R[x_1,x_2]+\mathbb R[x_2,x_3].\] Consequently, an architecture whose polynomial terms must each be supported in one of these blocks cannot represent \(x_1x_3\). More generally, an interaction whose variable support is contained in no block lies outside the prescribed sum of local polynomial rings unless an algebraic identity eliminates that interaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cross-block interaction unsupported by every block cannot be assembled from block-local polynomial terms.
assumptions_latex: All allowed polynomial terms belong to one of the two local polynomial rings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_1x_3\notin\mathbb R[x_{I_1}]+\mathbb R[x_{I_2}].

notation.meaning: Polynomial ring supported on block I_k.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsupported-Cross-Block Polynomial Obstruction
Sparse-Decomposition Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete cyclic-overlap obstruction to globally coherent local equality systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the blocks \(I_{12}=\{1,2\}\), \(I_{23}=\{2,3\}\), and \(I_{13}=\{1,3\}\), and the local equality ideals \[J_{12}=\langle x_1^2-1,x_2^2-1,x_1-x_2\rangle,\quad J_{23}=\langle x_2^2-1,x_3^2-1,x_2-x_3\rangle,\] \[J_{13}=\langle x_1^2-1,x_3^2-1,x_1+x_3\rangle.\] The three-block family does not satisfy running intersection. Each local real variety is nonempty, and the contractions of the two relevant ideals to each one-variable overlap agree, but no point in \(\mathbb R^3\) satisfies all three local ideals simultaneously. Thus pairwise contraction consistency and local real feasibility need not assemble into global feasibility on a cyclic overlap pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a three-block cycle, the displayed local equality systems are individually feasible and agree on every pairwise overlap, yet they have no globally feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local real varieties are nonempty and pairwise contraction-consistent, but their joint real feasible set is empty.

notation.meaning: Equality ideal on the block indexed by \(a,b\).

children.title: Compact Basic Closed Sets
children.top_down_role: Compact feasible regions described by finitely many polynomial inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Compact Basic Closed Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional real polynomial inequality descriptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given polynomials \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), their basic closed semialgebraic set is \[K(g)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\geq0\text{ for }j=1,\ldots,m\}.\] It is a compact basic closed set when it is compact in the Euclidean topology. Because every polynomial is continuous, each set \(\{x:g_j(x)\geq0\}\) is closed, so \(K(g)\) is automatically closed. Consequently, in finite-dimensional Euclidean space, compactness of \(K(g)\) is equivalent to its boundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact basic closed set is a bounded feasible set defined by finitely many nonstrict polynomial inequalities; closedness follows automatically from continuity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The basic closed set \(K(g)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\geq0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) is compact exactly when it is bounded.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent Archimedeanity Conditions for a Quadratic Module
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Four equivalent formulations of the compactness or Archimedeanity condition used by Putinar-type certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]\), let \(K=\{\mathbf x:g_j(\mathbf x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) be compact, and let \(Q(g)\) be the generated quadratic module. The following are equivalent: (a) there exist \(p_1,\ldots,p_s\in Q(g)\) such that \(K\subseteq\{\mathbf x:p_j(\mathbf x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,s\}\), this containing set is compact, and \(\prod_{j\in J}p_j\in Q(g)\) for every \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,s\}\); (b) there exists \(u\in Q(g)\) such that \(\{\mathbf x:u(\mathbf x)\ge0\}\) is compact; (c) there exists \(N\in\mathbb N\) such that \(N-\|\mathbf x\|^2\in Q(g)\); (d) for every \(p\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]\), there exists \(N\in\mathbb N\) such that \(N+p\in Q(g)\) and \(N-p\in Q(g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a compact basic closed set, the quadratic module’s compact-level-set condition is equivalent to a finite product-closed compact description, containment of a ball polynomial, and the order-unit property that every polynomial is bounded above and below modulo the module.
assumptions_latex: K=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(\mathbf x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\text{ is compact}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Conditions (a), (b), (c), and (d) stated above are equivalent.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines degree-bounded polynomial positivity certificate cones for a compact basic semialgebraic set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) be compact, where \(g_j\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]\). For \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), set \(g_J=\prod_{j\in J}g_j\), with \(g_\varnothing=g_0=1\). For \(k\in\mathbb N\), define
\[
P_k(g)=\left\{\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}}\sigma_Jg_J:\sigma_J\in\Sigma[\mathbf x],\ \deg(\sigma_Jg_J)\le 2k\right\},
\]
\[
Q_k(g)=\left\{\sum_{j=0}^m\sigma_jg_j:\sigma_j\in\Sigma[\mathbf x],\ \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le 2k\right\}.
\]
These are convex cones contained in \(\mathbb R[\mathbf x]_{2k}\), identifiable with cones in \(\mathbb R^{s(2k)}\), where \(s(r)=\binom{n+r}{n}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a compact basic semialgebraic set, the kth truncated preordering consists of degree-at-most-2k SOS-weighted products of all subsets of the defining inequalities, while the kth truncated quadratic module uses only the individual inequalities and 1. Both are convex cones of polynomials of degree at most 2k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_k(g),Q_k(g)\text{ are convex cones contained in }\mathbb R[\mathbf x]_{2k}\cong\mathbb R^{\binom{n+2k}{n}}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Volume convergence of polynomial outer approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer approximation of the nonnegative level set of a quantified polynomial value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathbf K\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m be compact with \mathbf K_{\mathbf x}\neq\varnothing for every \mathbf x\in\mathbf B. Suppose \operatorname{vol}\{\mathbf x\in\mathbf B:\overline J_f(\mathbf x)=0\}=0. If p_k\geq f on every fiber and p_k\to\overline J_f in L_1(\mathbf B), define \mathbf D_f^k:=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbf B:p_k(\mathbf x)\geq0\}. Then \mathbf D_f^k\supseteq\mathbf D_f for every k and \operatorname{vol}(\mathbf D_f^k\setminus\mathbf D_f)\to0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the zero level set of the fiberwise supremum has measure zero, the nonnegative level sets of convergent polynomial majorants contain D_f and their excess volume tends to zero.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall k,\ \mathbf D_f^k\supseteq\mathbf D_f,\qquad \operatorname{vol}(\mathbf D_f^k\setminus\mathbf D_f)\xrightarrow[k\to\infty]{}0.

children.title: Ball-Constraint Certificates
children.top_down_role: Explicit bounding generators used to establish an Archimedean description.

assumptions_latex: Let \(M=I(h)+Q(g)\subseteq\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) be an equality-augmented quadratic module.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any membership certificate \[R-\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2\in M\] with \(R>0\) certifies that \(M\) is Archimedean and that \(K(h,g)\) lies in the radius-\(\sqrt R\) ball.

notation.meaning: Equality-augmented quadratic module of the description.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit Euclidean-ball witness for an equality-augmented quadratic module.

source_refs.locator: 2.6.4 Quadratic modules for compact sets p. 74

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=I(h)+Q(g)\subseteq\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\). A ball-constraint certificate consists of a number \(R>0\) and an explicit ideal-plus-sums-of-squares representation proving \[R-\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2\in M.\] This membership is directly checkable by polynomial identities and positive-semidefinite Gram matrices for the sums of squares. It certifies the Archimedean property of \(M\). Moreover, every \(x\in K(h,g)\) makes every member of \(M\) nonnegative, so \(\sum_i x_i^2\leq R\); thus the feasible set is bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verified module representation of a ball polynomial certifies Archimedeanity and places every feasible point inside the stated Euclidean ball.

children.title: Coercive Module Members
children.top_down_role: Algebraic boundedness witnesses expressed through coercive members of a certificate cone.

assumptions_latex: Let \(M\subseteq\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) be a quadratic module nonnegative on its associated feasible set \(K_M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If a coercive polynomial \(u\) and constant \(C\) satisfy \(C-u\in M\), then \(K_M\subseteq\{x:u(x)\leq C\}\), so \(K_M\) is bounded and is compact when closed.

notation.meaning: The set on which every member of \(M\) is nonnegative.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coercive sublevel-set witnesses of boundedness for quadratic-module positivity sets.

source_refs.locator: 2.6.4 Quadratic modules for compact sets p. 74

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\subseteq\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) be a quadratic module, and let \(K_M\) be the set where all elements of \(M\) are nonnegative. A coercive-module boundedness certificate is a polynomial \(u\) satisfying \(u(x)\to+\infty\) as \(\|x\|_2\to\infty\), together with \(C\in\mathbb R\) such that \[C-u\in M.\] For every \(x\in K_M\), membership gives \(u(x)\leq C\). The sublevel set \(\{x:u(x)\leq C\}\) is compact, so it contains \(K_M\). This certifies boundedness, although conversion to the standard ball-membership form may require an additional algebraic argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A module element of the form constant minus a coercive polynomial confines the feasible set to a compact sublevel set and certifies boundedness.
knowledge_statements.title: Coercive Module Members

In particular, if \(u\) is coercive and \(C-u\in M\), then \(M\) is Archimedean because \(\{x:C-u(x)\ge0\}\) is compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic module containing a polynomial with compact nonnegative locus is Archimedean; constant minus a coercive polynomial is such a member.

children.title: Order-Unit Interpretations
children.top_down_role: Ordered-algebra formulations of Archimedeanity beyond a particular generator syntax.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Order-Unit Gauge of a Quadratic Module
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gauge formulation of symmetric algebraic order boundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be a unital commutative real algebra and \(M\subseteq A\) a quadratic module. Define the extended-valued gauge \[\|a\|_M:=\inf\{r\ge0:r1-a\in M\ \text{and}\ r1+a\in M\}.\] The unit \(1\) order-bounds every element of \(A\) exactly when \(\|a\|_M<\infty\) for every \(a\in A\). When finite everywhere, this gauge is an order seminorm; it need not separate distinct algebra elements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The order-unit property is equivalently finiteness everywhere of the symmetric order gauge induced by the quadratic module.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a unital commutative real algebra.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(1\) is an order unit if and only if \(\|a\|_M<\infty\) for every \(a\in A\).

notation.meaning: Extended-valued order-unit gauge induced by the module

knowledge_statements.title: Order-Unit Gauge of a Quadratic Module

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered-algebra definition and symmetric boundedness formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be a unital commutative real algebra and \(M\subseteq A\) a quadratic module. Write \(a\le_M b\) when \(b-a\in M\). The module is Archimedean precisely when its unit is an order unit: \[\forall a\in A\ \exists N>0\quad -N1\le_M a\le_M N1,\] equivalently, \(N1-a\in M\) and \(N1+a\in M\). Under this convention the condition is the ordered-algebra formulation of Archimedeanity, independent of a particular generator syntax.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic module is Archimedean exactly when the algebraic unit symmetrically order-bounds every algebra element.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a unital commutative real algebra.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) is Archimedean if and only if \(1\) is an order unit for \(\le_M\).

notation.meaning: Order induced by membership of the difference in M

knowledge_statements.title: Archimedeanity as an Order-Unit Property

assumptions_latex: Let \(A\) be a unital commutative real algebra and \(M\subseteq A\) a quadratic module.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The module \(M\) is Archimedean exactly when \(1\) is an order unit for the order induced by \(M\): \[\forall a\in A\ \exists N>0\quad N1+a\in M\ \text{and}\ N1-a\in M.\]

notation.meaning: Order defined by \(a\leq_M b\) exactly when \(b-a\in M\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered-algebra formulation for unital real algebras and quadratic modules.

source_refs.locator: 2.6.4 Quadratic modules for compact sets p. 74

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be a unital commutative real algebra and \(M\subseteq A\) a quadratic module. Define \(a\leq_M b\) when \(b-a\in M\). The unit \(1\) is an order unit if every \(a\in A\) is bounded above and below by a scalar multiple of \(1\): \[\forall a\in A\ \exists N>0\quad N1-a\in M\quad\text{and}\quad N1+a\in M.\] The quadratic module is Archimedean precisely when this order-unit condition holds. For \(A=\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), it is equivalent to the usual algebraic boundedness condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic module is Archimedean exactly when its unit order-bounds every algebra element from above and below.
knowledge_statements.title: Order-Unit Interpretations

children.title: Description Dependence of Archimedeanity
children.top_down_role: Variation of the Archimedean property across different descriptions of the same geometric set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General counterexample construction showing that Archimedeanity is a property of a chosen quadratic-module presentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g\) describe a bounded basic closed set \(K(g)\), and suppose \(Q(g)\) is not Archimedean. Choose \(R\) with \(\|x\|_2^2\le R\) on \(K(g)\), and set \(g'=(g,R-\|x\|_2^2)\). Then \(K(g')=K(g)\), while \(Q(g')\) is Archimedean and \(Q(g)\) is not. Thus every bounded non-Archimedean presentation generates a pair of descriptions of the same set with different Archimedean status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Appending a valid ball inequality to any bounded non-Archimedean presentation leaves its set unchanged but makes the enlarged module Archimedean, producing a general same-set counterexample family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K(g')=K(g),\qquad Q(g')\text{ is Archimedean},\qquad Q(g)\text{ is not Archimedean}.

notation.meaning: quadratic module generated by the presentation \(g\)
presentation obtained by adjoining a valid ball generator

knowledge_statements.title: Same-Set Archimedeanity-Separation Family

assumptions_latex: Let \(g\) and \(g'\) be finite polynomial descriptions satisfying \(K(g)=K(g')\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality of feasible sets does not by itself imply that \(Q(g)\) is Archimedean exactly when \(Q(g')\) is; adjoining a redundant generator \(R-\|x\|_2^2\) to any bounded description makes the enlarged module Archimedean.

notation.meaning: Quadratic module generated by the tuple \(g\).
Basic closed feasible set described by \(g\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generator dependence of quadratic-module Archimedeanity for a fixed feasible set.

source_refs.locator: 2.6.4 Quadratic modules for compact sets p. 74

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a polynomial tuple \(g\), Archimedeanity is a property of the generated quadratic module \(Q(g)\), not solely of the geometric set \(K(g)\). Thus two tuples \(g\) and \(g'\) may satisfy \(K(g)=K(g')\) without their modules having the same Archimedean status. If the common set is bounded, choose \(R>0\) with \(K(g)\subseteq\{x:\|x\|_2^2\leq R\}\). Adjoining the redundant generator \(R-\|x\|_2^2\) leaves the feasible set unchanged and makes the enlarged quadratic module Archimedean by construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Archimedeanity depends on the chosen generators, not only the feasible set; adding a redundant valid ball inequality repairs any bounded description.
knowledge_statements.title: Description Dependence of Archimedeanity

children.title: Archimedeanity-to-Compactness Principle

assumptions_latex: Let \(M=I(h)+Q(g)\subseteq\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) contain \(R-\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2\) for some \(R>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The associated feasible set \(K(h,g)\) is contained in \(\{x:\|x\|_2^2\leq R\}\) and is therefore compact.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=I(h)+Q(g)\subseteq\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) be Archimedean in the ball-certificate sense, so that for some \(R>0\), \[R-\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2\in M.\] Every element of \(M\) is nonnegative at every \(x\in K(h,g)\). Evaluating the displayed member therefore gives \(\sum_i x_i^2\leq R\), so \(K(h,g)\) is bounded. The set is also closed because it is defined by polynomial equalities and nonstrict inequalities. Hence \(K(h,g)\) is compact in \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An Archimedean ball certificate bounds every feasible point; polynomial constraints also make the feasible set closed, hence compact.

knowledge_statements.title: Compact Sets with Non-Archimedean Descriptions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates geometric compactness from Archimedeanity of a particular polynomial description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For generators \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\subset\mathbb{R}[x]\), let \(K(g)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_i(x)\ge 0\text{ for all }i\}\) and \(M(g)=\{\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i:\sigma_i\text{ are sums of squares}\}\). Compactness of \(K(g)\) does not imply Archimedeanity of \(M(g)\): there exist finite generator families for which \(K(g)\) is compact but, for every \(R>0\), \(R-\lVert x\rVert_2^2\notin M(g)\). Thus Archimedeanity depends on the selected generators, not only on their feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact basic semialgebraic set can have a chosen quadratic-module description that contains no algebraic ball constraint and is therefore non-Archimedean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compactness of \(K(g)\) alone does not ensure that \(M(g)\) is Archimedean.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compactness Makes the Full Preordering Archimedean
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contrast between a potentially non-Archimedean generated quadratic module and the full preordering of the same compact presentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K(g)\) be compact and let \(T(g)\) be the full preordering generated by \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\). For any \(R>\max_{x\in K(g)}\|x\|_2^2\), the polynomial \(R-\|x\|_2^2\) is strictly positive on \(K(g)\), and Schmüdgen's theorem yields \(R-\|x\|_2^2\in T(g)\). Thus \(T(g)\) is Archimedean even though the smaller quadratic module \(M(g)\) need not be.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact basic closed set, the full preordering contains a ball polynomial even when the selected quadratic module does not.
assumptions_latex: \(T(g)\) is the full preordering generated by the finite family \(g\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists R>0:\ R-\|x\|_2^2\in T(g),\quad\text{while compactness need not imply }R-\|x\|_2^2\in M(g).

notation.meaning: Full preordering generated by square-free products of the inequalities.
Quadratic module generated by the individual inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Bounding-Generator Repairs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repairs a description when boundedness is known independently of its generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K(g)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and suppose a verified bound \(K(g)\subseteq\{x:\lVert x\rVert_2^2\le R\}\) is available for some \(R>0\). Add the redundant generator \(g_{m+1}(x)=R-\lVert x\rVert_2^2\). Then \(K(g_1,\ldots,g_m,g_{m+1})=K(g)\), while the augmented quadratic module contains \(R-\lVert x\rVert_2^2\) and is therefore Archimedean. The repair changes the certificate cone without changing the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a valid redundant ball inequality preserves the feasible set and makes the augmented quadratic module Archimedean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented feasible set equals \(K(g)\), and its quadratic module is Archimedean.

knowledge_statements.title: Schmüdgen Compact-Preordering Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schmüdgen’s strict-positivity theorem for compact basic closed sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_1,\ldots,g_m,f\in\mathbb{R}[x]\), and define \(K(g)=\{x:g_i(x)\ge0\text{ for }1\le i\le m\}\). If \(K(g)\) is compact and \(f(x)>0\) for every \(x\in K(g)\), then \(f\) belongs to the preordering generated by \(g\): \[f=\sum_{\alpha\in\{0,1\}^m}\sigma_\alpha g_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots g_m^{\alpha_m},\] where every \(\sigma_\alpha\) is a sum-of-squares polynomial. No Archimedean hypothesis on the smaller quadratic module \(M(g)\) is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact basic closed set, every strictly positive polynomial has a Schmüdgen certificate using sums of squares times squarefree generator products.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\in T(g)\), the preordering generated by \(g\).

notation.meaning: Preordering generated by all squarefree products of the generators.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between Schmüdgen's guaranteed preordering membership and mere nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K(g)\) be compact and let \(T(g)\) be the preordering generated by \(g\). Schmüdgen's theorem guarantees \(f\in T(g)\) when \(f>0\) on \(K(g)\). Mere nonnegativity does not guarantee \(f\in T(g)\) in general. If \(f\ge0\) on \(K(g)\), however, then \(f+\varepsilon\in T(g)\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compactness guarantees preordering certificates for strictly positive polynomials; a merely nonnegative polynomial is guaranteed only epsilon-perturbed certificates in general.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\varepsilon>0,\ f+\varepsilon\in T(g),\quad\text{whereas }f\in T(g)\text{ need not hold}.

knowledge_statements.title: Putinar Archimedean Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Putinar’s strict-positivity theorem for an Archimedean quadratic module.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_1,\ldots,g_m,f\in\mathbb{R}[x]\), with quadratic module \(M(g)=\{\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i:\sigma_i\in\Sigma[x]\}\) and feasible set \(K(g)=\{x:g_i(x)\ge0\text{ for all }i\}\). If \(M(g)\) is Archimedean and \(f(x)>0\) for every \(x\in K(g)\), then \[f=\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i\] for sums-of-squares polynomials \(\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict positivity on the feasible set yields a quadratic-module certificate whenever the module generated by the constraints is Archimedean.

notation.meaning: Quadratic module generated by the constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between Putinar's guaranteed membership and mere nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M(g)\) be Archimedean. Putinar's theorem guarantees \(f\in M(g)\) when \(f>0\) on \(K(g)\). Replacing strict positivity by \(f\ge0\) is not valid in general: nonnegative polynomials that vanish on \(K(g)\) need not belong to \(M(g)\). Nevertheless, every \(f\ge0\) on \(K(g)\) satisfies \(f+\varepsilon\in M(g)\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Archimedeanity guarantees membership for strictly positive polynomials, not all nonnegative ones; every positive epsilon perturbation of a nonnegative polynomial is certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\varepsilon>0,\ f+\varepsilon\in M(g),\quad\text{whereas }f\in M(g)\text{ need not hold}.

notation.meaning: quadratic module generated by the constraints

children.title: Jacobi Archimedean Representation Regime
children.top_down_role: Ordered-algebra extension of Archimedean positivity representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epsilon-perturbed boundary form of Jacobi's Archimedean representation principle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be a commutative unital real algebra, let \(M\subseteq A\) be an Archimedean quadratic module, and let \(X_M\) be the set of unital algebra homomorphisms \(\varphi:A\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(\varphi(M)\subseteq\mathbb R_{\ge0}\). If \(\varphi(a)\ge0\) for every \(\varphi\in X_M\), then \[a+\varepsilon1\in M\qquad\text{for every }\varepsilon>0.\] No unperturbed membership conclusion is asserted when \(a\) has zeros on \(X_M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Jacobi's Archimedean hypotheses, characterwise nonnegativity implies module membership after every positive scalar perturbation.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a commutative unital real algebra.
\(M\subseteq A\) is an Archimedean quadratic module.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a+\varepsilon1\in M\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\).

notation.meaning: Unital characters nonnegative on the module

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonnegativity Gives Only Approximate Membership in General
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary between strict positivity and characterwise nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the hypotheses of the Jacobi Archimedean Representation Theorem, \(\varphi(a)\ge0\) on \(X_M\) guarantees \(a+\varepsilon1\in M\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\). It does not generally guarantee \(a\in M\): Archimedean quadratic modules need not be closed in the finest locally convex topology, and in such modules there are elements in \(\overline M\setminus M\), equivalently elements nonnegative on \(X_M\) that lack unperturbed membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Characterwise nonnegativity yields every positive scalar perturbation as a certificate, but unperturbed membership can fail for a nonclosed Archimedean module.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a commutative unital real algebra.
The failure assertion concerns Archimedean modules that are not closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a+\varepsilon1\in M\) for all \(\varepsilon>0\), while \(a\in M\) is not valid as a universal conclusion.

notation.meaning: Closure of M in the finest locally convex topology

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict-positivity representation in a commutative unital real algebra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be a commutative unital real algebra and \(M\subseteq A\) an Archimedean quadratic module. Define \[X_M=\{\varphi:A\to\mathbb R:\varphi\text{ is a unital algebra homomorphism and }\varphi(m)\ge0\ \forall m\in M\}.\] If \(a\in A\) satisfies \(\varphi(a)>0\) for every \(\varphi\in X_M\), then \(a\in M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict positivity on every character compatible with an Archimedean quadratic module implies membership in that module.

\(M\subseteq A\) is an Archimedean quadratic module.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Jacobi’s representation theorem in a commutative unital real algebra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be a commutative unital real algebra and \(M\subseteq A\) an Archimedean quadratic module. knowledge_statements.title: Compact-Theorem Applicability Comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares the assumptions and certificate cones of three strict-positivity regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K(g)=\{x:g_i(x)\ge0\}\), compactness of \(K(g)\) suffices for Schmüdgen’s conclusion \(f\in T(g)\) whenever \(f>0\) on \(K(g)\). Putinar’s smaller certificate \(f\in M(g)\) requires the stronger, description-dependent assumption that \(M(g)\) is Archimedean, which itself implies compactness of \(K(g)\). Jacobi’s theorem replaces the polynomial ring and point set by a commutative unital real algebra and its module-compatible character space. Since \(M(g)\subseteq T(g)\), the stronger Putinar hypothesis yields certificates in a smaller cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Schmüdgen uses compactness and a larger preordering; Putinar uses Archimedeanity and a smaller module; Jacobi extends the Archimedean principle to real algebras.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Schmüdgen, Putinar, and Jacobi differ in ambient algebra, hypotheses, and certificate-container size.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform bounded-degree positivity certification for affine polynomials on a compact basic semialgebraic set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a compact basic semialgebraic set defined by \(g\). The P-BDR property holds for \(K\) if there exist \(d\in\mathbb N\) and a Lebesgue-null set \(N\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) such that every affine polynomial \(f(x)=f_0+f_1^Tx\) satisfying \(f>0\) on \(K\) and \(f_1\notin N\) belongs to \(Q_d(g)\). The integer \(d\) is called its order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact basic semialgebraic set has P-BDR when, apart from a possible measure-zero set of affine slope vectors, every affine polynomial strictly positive on the set has a Putinar certificate of one uniform bounded order.
assumptions_latex: K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is compact and defined by }g
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists d\in\mathbb N\ \exists N\subseteq\mathbb R^n,\ \lambda(N)=0:\quad f>0\text{ on }K,\ f_1\notin N\Longrightarrow f\in Q_d(g)
