knowledge_statements.title: Compact K-Moment Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact basic-closed support where preordering positivity suffices for moment representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\geq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) be compact, let \(T(g)\) be the preordering generated by \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\), and let \(L:\mathbb R[x]\to\mathbb R\) be linear. Then \(L\) has a positive Borel representing measure supported on \(K\) if and only if \(L(t)\geq0\) for every \(t\in T(g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact basic closed set, a linear polynomial functional has a supported positive representing measure exactly when it is nonnegative on the generated preordering.

children.title: Noncompact Moment Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Noncompact Moment Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Carleman-type growth condition restoring measure existence for positive moment data on an unbounded basic closed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{g_1\geq0,\ldots,g_m\geq0\}\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let \(L:\mathbb R[x]\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(L(p^2g_j)\geq0\) for every polynomial \(p\), with \(g_0=1\). If, for every coordinate \(i\), the Carleman divergence condition \(\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}L(x_i^{2k})^{-1/(2k)}=\infty\) holds, then \(L\) has a unique positive Borel representing measure \(\mu\) supported on \(K\). Without an appropriate growth or determinacy condition, positivity of the moment and localizing matrices alone need not supply this conclusion on an unbounded set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For unbounded supports, positive moment and localizing data plus coordinatewise Carleman divergence yield a unique supported representing measure.
assumptions_latex: The displayed Carleman series diverges for every coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists!\mu\geq0:\ \operatorname{supp}\mu\subseteq K\text{ and }L(p)=\int_Kp\,d\mu\ \forall p\in\mathbb R[x]\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordinatewise Carleman regime is plausible and the condition role fits the leaf, but the exact combination of localizing positivity, supported existence, and uniqueness requires a specific theorem locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Extension Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncated moment feasibility characterized through extension to a full support-positive functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed, let \(d\in\mathbb N\), and let \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\leq2d}\) define the truncated Riesz functional \(L_y\) on \(\mathbb R[x]_{2d}\). Then \(y\) has a positive Borel representing measure supported on \(K\) if and only if \(L_y\) admits a linear extension \(\widetilde L:\mathbb R[x]\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(\widetilde L(p)\geq0\) for every polynomial \(p\) that is nonnegative on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncated moment data have a supported positive representing measure exactly when their Riesz functional extends to a full functional positive on every polynomial nonnegative on the support.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\text{ has a }K\text{-representing measure}\iff L_y\text{ has a full }K\text{-positive extension }\widetilde L\).

full K-positive extension of the truncated functional

children.title: Flat-Extension Regime
children.top_down_role: Rank-stable truncated-moment regime supporting finite atomic representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Flat-Extension Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained multivariate flat-extension criterion for a truncated real moment sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le 2d}\) be a real truncated multisequence with \(y_0=1\), where \(d\ge 1\). If its moment matrix satisfies \(M_d(y)\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}M_d(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{d-1}(y)=r\), then \(y\) admits a representing probability measure \(\mu\) on \(\mathbb R^n\) having exactly \(r\) atoms. Moreover, \(y\) has a flat positive-semidefinite extension to every higher order, so integration against \(\mu\) reproduces all entries of the resulting full moment sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive semidefinite moment matrix whose rank stabilizes between two consecutive orders has a finitely atomic representing measure, with atom count equal to that rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_\alpha=\int x^\alpha\,d\mu(x)\) for \(|\alpha|\le2d\), where \(\mu\) is an \(r\)-atomic probability measure.

notation.meaning: moment matrix indexed by monomials of degree at most d
stable moment-matrix rank and number of atoms

knowledge_statements.title: Nonextendable Truncated Sequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A univariate positive truncated moment matrix that has no positive extension or representing measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the degree-four univariate sequence \(y=(y_0,y_1,y_2,y_3,y_4)=(1,0,0,0,1)\). Its truncated moment matrix is \[M_2(y)=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&0&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\] Nevertheless, no positive-semidefinite moment extension through degree six exists. Indeed, in any candidate \(M_3\), the diagonal entry indexed by \(x\) is \(y_2=0\); positive semidefiniteness would force its entire row to vanish, whereas its entry against \(x^3\) equals \(y_4=1\). Consequently, \(y\) has no representing positive measure on \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sequence (1,0,0,0,1) has a positive semidefinite degree-four moment matrix but cannot extend positively and has no representing measure.
assumptions_latex: Moment matrices use the Hankel convention \(M_d(y)_{i,j}=y_{i+j}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_2(y)\succeq0\), but no \(M_3(\widetilde y)\succeq0\) can extend it and no representing positive measure exists.

notation.meaning: univariate Hankel moment matrix of order d
a putative higher-degree extension of y

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample kind fits this failure-oriented leaf. The displayed Hankel matrix and the zero-diagonal PSD obstruction are internally consistent, but no inspectable source supports the example or its nonextendability conclusion.

children.title: Strict-Feasibility Regimes
children.top_down_role: Interior-point conditions supporting standard conic duality conclusions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative Slater Condition on the Effective Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict-feasibility formulation for a cone in a proper span or known face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), primal relative strict feasibility means that a feasible \(\bar x\) lies in \(\operatorname{ri}K\), the ordinary interior relative to \(\operatorname{span}K\). If a known face \(F\) contains every feasible point, the corresponding reduced condition is \(\bar x\in\operatorname{ri}F\). Requiring ambient interior is unnecessarily strong for a non-full-dimensional cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slater feasibility uses the relative interior of the effective cone or face, not ambient interior.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone in a finite-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\bar x:A\bar x=b,\ \bar x\in\operatorname{ri}K\quad\text{is primal relative Slater feasibility}.

notation.meaning: Interior of K relative to its span.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Slater Condition on the Effective Cone

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Absence of Slater Is Not a Duality-Gap Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict feasibility is sufficient but not necessary for regular finite-order behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Failure of primal and dual strict feasibility removes the standard Slater guarantee but does not imply a positive gap or nonattainment. For example, the feasibility system \(x=0\), \(x\in\mathbb R_+\), has no feasible point in \(\operatorname{ri}\mathbb R_+\), while its unique feasible point is attained and the problem has no intrinsic value gap. Closedness or facial analysis is needed to diagnose an actual duality failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The absence of Slater alone proves neither a gap nor nonattainment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \neg\mathrm{Slater}\not\Longrightarrow\text{duality gap or nonattainment}.
knowledge_statements.title: Absence of Slater Is Not a Duality-Gap Certificate
Strict-Feasibility Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conic strong duality under primal or dual Slater feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq E\) be a closed convex cone, and consider \[p^*=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\},\qquad d^*=\sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:c-A^*y\in K^*\}.\] If the primal value is finite and there exists \(\bar x\in\operatorname{ri}K\) with \(A\bar x=b\), then \(p^*=d^*\) and the dual optimum is attained. Symmetrically, if the dual value is finite and some \(\bar y\) satisfies \(c-A^*\bar y\in\operatorname{ri}K^*\), then \(p^*=d^*\) and the primal optimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite conic program has zero duality gap and opposite-side attainment when either its primal or dual system is strictly feasible.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is finite-dimensional and \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone
The corresponding primal or dual Slater point exists
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*=d^*\), with attainment on the side opposite the stated strict-feasibility condition.

notation.meaning: relative interior of K in its span
adjoint of the linear map A

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits the strict-feasibility leaf. The result resembles finite-dimensional conic Slater duality, but an authoritative source is needed to verify that relative interior in the cone's span is sufficient in the stated formulation and that the finiteness and attainment hypotheses are correctly paired.

children.title: Closed Value-Cones
children.top_down_role: Closedness conditions relevant to dual attainment and separation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonclosed Linear Image of the PSD Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite example showing that closedness is not preserved by linear projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\mathbb S_+^2\) and \(L(X)=(X_{11},2X_{12})\). Then \[L(K)=\{(a,b):a>0,\ b\in\mathbb R\}\cup\{(0,0)\}.\] Thus \((1/k,1)\in L(K)\) converges to \((0,1)\notin L(K)\), so a linear image of a closed positive-semidefinite cone need not be closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting the two-by-two PSD cone onto one diagonal and one off-diagonal coordinate yields a nonclosed cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L(K)\text{ is not closed}.

notation.meaning: Cone of two-by-two positive-semidefinite symmetric matrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Linear Image of the PSD Cone

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-function interpretation of the closed upper image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(u)=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=u,\ x\in K\}\), with \(v(u)=+\infty\) for an empty fiber. If every finite fiber infimum is attained, then \(\mathcal V=\{(u,t):t\ge v(u)\}=\operatorname{epi}v\), and \(\mathcal V\) is closed exactly when \(v\) is lower semicontinuous. Without fiber attainment, the attainable upper image can omit points on the epigraph boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With fiber attainment, the closed upper value image is exactly the epigraph of a lower-semicontinuous value function.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone in a finite-dimensional space.
Every finite fiber value is attained for the epigraph equality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal V=\operatorname{epi}v,\qquad\mathcal V\text{ closed}\Longleftrightarrow v\text{ lower semicontinuous}.

notation.meaning: Perturbation value function at right-hand side u.

knowledge_statements.title: Value-Cone Closure and Lower-Semicontinuity
Closed Value-Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closedness criterion for separating an infeasible objective bound from attainable conic values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the conic system \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), define the value cone \[\mathcal V=\{(Ax,\langle c,x\rangle+s):x\in K,\ s\ge0\}.\] If \(\mathcal V\) is closed, then every scalar \(\gamma<p^*\) yields \((b,\gamma)\notin\mathcal V\), and strong separation produces \((y,\eta)\) with \(\eta>0\). After normalization, this separator is dual feasible and certifies \(\langle b,y\rangle>\gamma\). Hence closedness prevents loss of limiting value pairs and supplies dual certificates arbitrarily close to the primal value; with finite \(p^*\), it yields equality of primal and dual values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closedness of the conic value image lets separation certify every strict lower bound and thereby rules out a duality gap.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone in a finite-dimensional space
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^*=p^*\), and every \(\gamma<p^*\) has a dual-feasible certificate with value exceeding \(\gamma\).

notation.meaning: upper value cone of constraint images and objective values

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the closed-value-cone leaf. The critical claim that separation necessarily yields a separator with strictly positive objective coefficient, permitting normalization to a dual-feasible point, requires additional hypotheses or a cited theorem. No source reference is supplied.

children.title: Facial-Reduction Regimes
children.top_down_role: Lower-dimensional conic structure arising when strict feasibility is absent.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum number of admitted facial-reduction cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible conic system whose minimal containing face \(F_{\min}\) is reachable by valid exposing cuts, its singularity degree is the least \(t\ge0\) for which \(K=F_0\supsetneq F_1\supsetneq\cdots\supsetneq F_t=F_{\min}\) is such a facial-reduction chain. It is zero exactly when the original system has a feasible point in \(\operatorname{ri}K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Singularity degree counts the fewest exposing cuts required to reach the feasible set's minimal face.
assumptions_latex: The minimal face is reachable by the admitted facial-reduction certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{sd}=0\Longleftrightarrow\exists x\in\operatorname{ri}K\text{ with }Ax=b.

notation.meaning: Minimal cone face containing the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Singularity Degree

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limitation of the exposing-vector facial-reduction algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an arbitrary closed convex cone, a proper minimal face need not be obtainable by the stated finite sequence of exposed-face cuts without an additional facial-exposure or certificate-reachability hypothesis. Polyhedral and positive-semidefinite cones satisfy the standard exposed-face structure used by facial reduction, whereas a general cone may require a more qualified formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite exposing-vector reduction to the minimal face requires a suitable cone class or an explicit reachability assumption.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in finite dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Closed convexity alone does not justify the asserted exposing chain to }F_{\min}.
knowledge_statements.title: Exposure Boundary for General Cones

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity restored on the minimal face without changing the feasible problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_{\min}\) be the minimal face of \(K\) containing a nonempty affine conic feasible set \(\mathcal F\). Then \(\mathcal F\cap\operatorname{ri}F_{\min}\ne\varnothing\). Replacing \(K\) by \(F_{\min}\) leaves \(\mathcal F\) and every objective value on it unchanged while making the reduced system relatively strictly feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restriction to the minimal face preserves the problem and restores relative strict feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The conic feasible set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal F=\{x:Ax=b,\ x\in F_{\min}\},\qquad\mathcal F\cap\operatorname{ri}F_{\min}\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Relative-Slater Equivalence
Facial-Reduction Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facial reduction restores relative strict feasibility on the minimal cone face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a feasible system \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), initialize \(F_0=K\). While no feasible point lies in \(\operatorname{ri}F_i\), choose an exposing vector \(z_i\in F_i^*\setminus F_i^\perp\) satisfying \(\langle z_i,x\rangle=0\) for every feasible \(x\), and set \(F_{i+1}=F_i\cap z_i^\perp\). Stop at the first index \(t\) for which some feasible \(\bar x\in\operatorname{ri}F_t\) exists. The output \(F_t\) is the minimal face of \(K\) containing the feasible set, and the reduced conic formulation over \(F_t\) satisfies relative Slater feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated exposing cuts replace the original cone by the minimal face containing all feasible points, where relative strict feasibility holds.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional space
Each nonminimal current face admits the stated exposing vector
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure terminates after finitely many strict face reductions at the minimal face \(F_t\), with a feasible point in \(\operatorname{ri}F_t\).

notation.meaning: orthogonal complement of the span of the current face

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind appropriately captures facial reduction. Its finite termination and minimal-face conclusion are plausible under the explicit exposing-vector assumption, but that assumption can fail for general closed convex cones and must be checked against a source or specialized cone class.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong duality and barycentric recovery from optimal SOS densities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combines dual attainment and complementarity with convex barycentric recovery and its accumulation-point guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume f^*>-\infty and \operatorname{int}K\neq\varnothing. For every order d, the scalar moment-localizing SDP and its SOS-density dual have no duality gap, and the dual has an optimizer \sigma_d^*\in\Sigma[x]_d satisfying \int_K(f-\lambda_d)\sigma_d^*\,d\mu=0. If K and f are convex and x_d^*:=\int_K x\sigma_d^*\,d\mu, then x_d^*\in K and f^*\leq f(x_d^*)\leq\lambda_d, hence f(x_d^*)\to f^*. If, additionally, \{x\in K:f(x)\leq f_0\} is compact for some f_0>f^*, every accumulation point \bar x\in K of (x_d^*) satisfies f(\bar x)=f^*.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With nonempty interior, the upper-bound SDP and its SOS-density dual have equal values, the dual optimum is attained, and an integral complementarity identity holds. When the set and objective are convex, the mean of the optimal density is feasible and has objective value between the optimum and the hierarchy bound. These values converge to the optimum; under a compact near-optimal sublevel set, every accumulation point is a global minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \text{for accumulation-point optimality: }\exists f_0>f^*\text{ such that }\{x\in K:f(x)\leq f_0\}\text{ is compact}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_d^*=\lambda_d,\quad \exists\sigma_d^*\in\Sigma[x]_d:\int_K(f-\lambda_d)\sigma_d^*\,d\mu=0;\quad x_d^*\in K,\ f^*\leq f(x_d^*)\leq\lambda_d\to f^*;\quad x_{d_j}^*\to\bar x\Rightarrow f(\bar x)=f^*.

children.title: Finite-Order Duality Failures
children.top_down_role: Nonattainment and duality-gap boundaries at truncated certificate orders.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite SDP Infimum Without Primal Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit finite-dimensional semidefinite nonattainment example.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\inf_{x,y}\left\{x:\begin{pmatrix}x&1\\1&y\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\right\}.\] Feasibility is equivalent to \(x\ge0\), \(y\ge0\), and \(xy\ge1\). Every \(x>0\) is feasible with \(y=1/x\), so the infimum is zero, but no feasible matrix has \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-by-two SDP has a finite infimum approached by unbounded feasible matrices but no optimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^*=0\quad\text{and the primal infimum is not attained}.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite SDP Infimum Without Primal Attainment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinct failure modes at one finite relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite values \(q_d\le p_d\), a value-gap failure means \(q_d<p_d\). Dual nonattainment means no dual-feasible certificate realizes the finite supremum \(q_d\), and primal nonattainment means no primal-feasible point realizes the finite infimum \(p_d\). Equality \(q_d=p_d\) is logically independent of attainment on either side.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive gap, primal nonattainment, and dual certificate nonattainment are separate finite-order failures.
assumptions_latex: The order-\(d\) primal and dual values are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q_d=p_d\not\Longrightarrow\text{primal or dual attainment}.
knowledge_statements.title: Gap and Attainment Failure Taxonomy

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Asymptotic Convergence Does Not Repair a Fixed Order
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of hierarchy limits from finite-order conic regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even if \(p_d\to f^*\) and \(q_d\to f^*\) as \(d\to\infty\), these limits imply neither equality nor attainment at a prescribed index \(d_0\). Finite-order conclusions must follow from the conic pair at \(d_0\), such as through Slater regularity, closed-value-cone arguments, or valid facial reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergence of hierarchy values cannot substitute for regularity of a particular finite SDP.
assumptions_latex: Both hierarchy value sequences converge to the same limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_d,q_d\to f^*\not\Longrightarrow p_{d_0}=q_{d_0}\text{ or attainment at }d_0.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Convergence Does Not Repair a Fixed Order
Finite-Order Duality Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure modes of a fixed truncated moment–certificate conic pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At relaxation order \(d\), let \(p_d\) be the moment-primal value and \(q_d\) the polynomial-certificate dual value, with weak duality \(q_d\le p_d\). Standard finite-order duality fails whenever \(q_d<p_d\), or whenever \(q_d=p_d\) but the certificate supremum is not attained. Such behavior can occur when neither conic side is relatively strictly feasible and the associated linear value cone is nonclosed. Thus asymptotic convergence of \(p_d\) and \(q_d\) as \(d\to\infty\) does not itself imply zero gap or certificate attainment at any specified finite order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed relaxation order, a positive gap or an unattained certificate optimum is a duality failure; asymptotic convergence does not exclude either event.
assumptions_latex: \(p_d\) and \(q_d\) form a finite-dimensional conic primal–dual pair
No finite-order regularity assumption is imposed
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite-order strong duality requires both \(p_d=q_d\) and attainment of the relevant certificate optimum; asymptotic convergence alone is insufficient.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind exactly fits this leaf, and the distinction between a gap, nonattainment, and asymptotic convergence is appropriate. A source or explicit cited example is still required, especially for the assertion that these failures can arise from simultaneous lack of relative strict feasibility and nonclosedness of the value cone.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite convergence under finitely many positive-definite minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient regime for finite exactness and primal-dual attainment in the moment-SOS hierarchy for convex polynomial programs; the source-referenced Assumption 2.14 is retained explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), where \(f\) and every \(-g_j\) are convex. Assume that Assumption 2.14 and Slater's condition hold, that the global minimizers in \(K\) are finite in number, and that \(\nabla^2f(x^*)\succ0\) at every global minimizer \(x^*\). Then there exists an index \(d\) such that \(f^*=\rho_d^*=\rho_d\), and both corresponding semidefinite relaxations have optimal solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumption 2.14, Slater's condition, and positive-definite objective Hessians at finitely many global minimizers, the primal-dual moment-SOS hierarchy becomes exact at a finite order and both relaxations attain their optima.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists d\quad f^*=\rho_d^*=\rho_d,\quad\text{and both corresponding order-}d\text{ relaxations attain their optima}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic-module certificate from convexity and positive-definite optimal curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded sufficient conditions for a finite SOS quadratic-module certificate in the source polynomial-optimization setup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbf K\) and \(Q(g)\) be as in the source setup. Suppose Assumption 2.14 and Slater's condition hold, \(f\) and \(-g_j\) are convex for \(j=1,\ldots,m\), and \(f\) has finitely many minimizers on \(\mathbf K\). If the Hessian of the Lagrangian is positive definite at every minimizer \(\mathbf x^*\in\mathbf K\)—in particular, it suffices that \(\nabla^2 f(\mathbf x^*)\succ0\) at every minimizer—then \(f-f^*\in Q(g)\). Thus there exist SOS polynomials \(\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m\) such that \[f-f^*=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the source setup's standing assumption, Slater condition, convexity, finiteness of the minimizer set, and positive-definite Lagrangian curvature at every minimizer, the optimality gap has an SOS quadratic-module certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbf K\) and \(Q(g)\) are as in the source setup, and Assumption 2.14 holds.
At every minimizer \(\mathbf x^*\), the Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite; the stated sufficient special case is \(\nabla^2f(\mathbf x^*)\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f-f^*\in Q(g),\qquad f-f^*=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j,\quad \sigma_j\in\Sigma[\mathbf x].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial lifting and moment-SOS guarantees for basic semialgebraic objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the inherited polynomial descriptions of K, S, and the graph of f; the source specifies the finite-exactness hypothesis only as the requisite moment-matrix rank condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) have its given basic semialgebraic description, let \(S\) have a lifted description by equations \(u_k(x,y)=0\) and sign constraints \(y_k\ge 0\), and let \(f\in A\) be a basic semialgebraic function whose graph is represented by \(q_\ell(x,z)=0\) and \(z_j\ge0\), with \(z_{m_f}=f(x)\). Then \(\inf_{x\in S}f(x)=\inf\{z_{m_f}:(x,y,z)\in\Omega\}\), where \(\Omega\) is the resulting basic semialgebraic set defined by the constraints for \(K\), \(S\), and the graph of \(f\). If the redundant Archimedean constraint \(M-\|(x,y,z)\|^2\ge0\) is added, the optimal values \(\rho_d\) of the associated moment-SOS relaxations satisfy \(\rho_d\to f^*\). If, at an optimal solution of relaxation order \(d\), the requisite moment-matrix rank condition holds, then \(\rho_d=f^*\) and global minimizers can be extracted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph representation of a basic semialgebraic objective converts its minimization over a lifted semialgebraic feasible set exactly into polynomial optimization. Adding a redundant Archimedean ball constraint makes the moment-SOS relaxation values converge to the global optimum; the requisite moment-matrix rank condition at a relaxation order certifies finite exactness and permits extraction of global minimizers.
assumptions_latex: K\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ has the prescribed basic semialgebraic representation}
S\text{ has the prescribed lifted representation using }u_k(x,y)=0\text{ and }y_k\ge0
f\in A\text{ is basic semialgebraic with graph constraints }q_\ell(x,z)=0,\ z_j\ge0
M-\|(x,y,z)\|^2\ge0\text{ is added for the asymptotic convergence conclusion}
\text{The requisite moment-matrix rank condition holds at order }d\text{ for the finite-exactness conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f^*=\inf_{(x,y,z)\in\Omega}z_{m_f},\qquad \rho_d\to f^*,\qquad \text{and under the rank condition }\rho_d=f^*\text{ with extractable global minimizers.}

children.title: Finite Real-Variety Exactness
children.top_down_role: Finite-order exactness family tied to finitely many real equality solutions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Real Locus Without Exactness for the Original Ideal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows why finiteness alone does not guarantee an SOS-modulo-ideal certificate for a non-real-radical presentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=\langle x^2\rangle\subset\mathbb R[x]\) and minimize \(f(x)=x\) on \(V_{\mathbb R}(I)=\{0\}\). Then \(f_{\min}=0\), but \(x\notin\Sigma[x]+I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The finite real locus defined by x²=0 does not provide an SOS certificate modulo the original ideal for the objective x.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_{\mathbb R}(I)=\{0\}\) but \(f-f_{\min}=x\notin\Sigma[x]+I\).

notation.meaning: cone of sums of squares of real polynomials

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Real Locus Without Exactness for the Original Ideal

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-order equality-only SOS exactness without an unsupported general conic-regularity claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let I\subseteq\mathbb R[x] be real radical and let V_{\mathbb R}(I)=\{u_1,\ldots,u_s\}\ne\varnothing. For every f\in\mathbb R[x], with f^*=\min_i f(u_i), there exist polynomials p_1,\ldots,p_s and q\in I such that p_i(u_j)=\delta_{ij} and f-f^*=\sum_{i=1}^s\big(\sqrt{f(u_i)-f^*}\,p_i\big)^2+q. Consequently this identity lies in \Sigma[x]_{2d}+I_{2d} for some finite d, the equality-only SOS bound attains f^*, and a Dirac moment sequence at any minimizing u_i attains the corresponding moment value f^*.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a nonempty finite real variety represented by its real-radical ideal, interpolation expresses every objective gap as an SOS modulo the ideal at a finite degree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists d<\infty:\ f-f^*\in\Sigma[x]_{2d}+I_{2d},\quad \rho_d=f^*.

notation.meaning: Polynomial interpolating the indicator of u_i on the finite real variety.
Degree-2d truncation of the equality ideal.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Real-Radical Variety Interpolation Exactness
Finite Real-Variety Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convergence for equality-constrained optimization on a finite real variety.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_m\rangle\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) be real radical and suppose its real variety \(V_{\mathbb R}(I)\) is finite and nonempty. For every \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\), let \(f_{\min}=\min_{x\in V_{\mathbb R}(I)}f(x)\). Then there exist sums of squares \(\sigma\), polynomials \(\phi_i\), and an integer \(d\) such that \[f-f_{\min}=\sigma+\sum_{i=1}^m\phi_i h_i,\qquad \deg\sigma,\ \deg(\phi_i h_i)\le2d.\] Consequently, the order-\(d\) moment/SOS relaxation is exact and its dual certificate is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite real variety generated by a real-radical equality ideal, every polynomial optimization problem has an exact SOS relaxation at some finite order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For some finite \(d\), \(f-f_{\min}\in\Sigma[x]_{2d}+I_{2d}\), so the order-\(d\) relaxation value equals \(f_{\min}\).

notation.meaning: real zero set of the ideal I
sums of squares of degree at most 2d

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits the exactness leaf, and the finite real-radical variety hypothesis plausibly supports an SOS-mod-ideal representation. No source is provided for the representation theorem or for the additional conclusion that the stated moment/SOS dual certificate is attained at the same order.

children.title: Finite Semialgebraic-Set Exactness
children.top_down_role: Finite-order exactness family for finite feasible sets defined jointly by equalities and inequalities.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cardinality Alone Does Not Determine a Relaxation Order
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates finite feasible geometry from a numerical truncation bound for arbitrary objectives and presentations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\{x:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\geq0\}\), the fact that \(|K|<\infty\) does not by itself determine a relaxation order. A finite-degree certificate depends on the objective degree and on the degrees, multiplicities, redundancy, and vanishing relations represented by the chosen generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The size of a finite feasible set alone is not a degree or complexity bound for an arbitrary polynomial presentation.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is described by finitely many polynomial equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No relaxation-order bound follows from \(|K|\) alone over arbitrary objectives and presentations.
knowledge_statements.title: Cardinality Alone Does Not Determine a Relaxation Order

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singleton Sets with Unbounded Required Input Order
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fixed-cardinality family showing that feasible-set cardinality cannot bound relaxation order over arbitrary objective degrees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(r\ge1\), minimize \(f_r(x)=x^{2r}\) subject to \(h(x)=x=0\). The feasible set is the singleton \(K=\{0\}\) and \(f_r^*=0\). Under total-degree truncation at \(2d\), \(f_r\notin I_{2d}(h)+Q_d(\varnothing)\) for \(d<r\), whereas \(f_r\in I_{2r}(h)+Q_r(\varnothing)\). Thus the least certificate order is \(r\) although \(|K|=1\) for every \(r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Singleton feasible sets can require arbitrarily high relaxation order when objective degree grows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |K|=1\quad\text{and}\quad d_{\min}(f_r)=r.

notation.meaning: Least certificate order for the displayed presentation.

knowledge_statements.title: Singleton Sets with Unbounded Required Input Order
Finite Semialgebraic-Set Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite-feasible-set certificate condition guaranteeing exactness at a finite relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x:h_i(x)=0,\ g_j(x)\ge0\}\) be finite and nonempty, and let \(f_{\min}=\min_K f\). A finite semialgebraic exactness regime holds when there exists \(d\) such that \[f-f_{\min}\in I_{2d}(h)+Q_d(g),\] where \(I_{2d}(h)\) is the degree-\(2d\) truncation of the equality ideal and \(Q_d(g)\) is the degree-\(2d\) truncated quadratic module. This membership is a finite, checkable certificate and implies that both the order-\(d\) SOS bound and its moment dual value equal \(f_{\min}\), provided finite-order conic duality holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite feasible set, finite exactness is certified once the objective gap belongs to a finite-degree equality ideal plus quadratic module.
assumptions_latex: Finite-order conic duality holds at the certificate order
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(f-f_{\min}\in I_{2d}(h)+Q_d(g)\), then the order-\(d\) moment and SOS values equal \(f_{\min}\).

notation.meaning: truncated ideal generated by the equality constraints
truncated quadratic module generated by the inequalities

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is defensible because the record states a sufficient certificate-membership regime rather than claiming finiteness alone guarantees membership. It is mathematically conditional and therefore does not establish the stronger finite-set exactness family without further hypotheses; an authoritative locator is required for the exact primal-dual implication.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exactness After Adding the Vanishing Ideal of a Finite Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed equality-only interpolation theorem after replacing the mixed presentation by the full vanishing ideal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{u_1,\ldots,u_s\}\) be finite and nonempty. If the equality relations contain \(I(K)\), then every objective gap is a sum of squares modulo \(I(K)\), giving finite equality-based exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding every polynomial relation vanishing on a finite set permits an interpolation-based SOS representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f-f_{\min}\in\Sigma[x]+I(K)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exactness After Adding the Vanishing Ideal of a Finite Set

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns exactness questions for the original mixed finite-feasible-set presentation and the absence of a cardinality-only order bound. The proposed I(K) theorem is deferred as equality-variety exactness. Pure equality exactness and preordering refinement are excluded to sibling scopes.

children.title: Finite-Set Preordering Refinement
children.top_down_role: Preordering-based specialization when finiteness belongs to the full feasible set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarifies that finite-order preordering strength depends on the chosen inequality presentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Adding a redundant inequality can leave \(K\) unchanged while changing the generated preordering and its finite truncations by introducing new square-free products. Thus equal feasible sets need not have equal truncated preorderings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent descriptions of the same finite set can yield different finite-order preorderings.
assumptions_latex: Two inequality presentations define the same feasible set \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality of feasible sets does not imply equality of their truncated preorderings.
knowledge_statements.title: Generator Dependence of Preordering Truncations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural comparison of certificate cones at a common truncation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed inequality generators \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\) and a common degree convention, the truncated preordering contains the truncated quadratic module because it includes the square-free products indexed by \(0,e_1,\ldots,e_m\). Hence \(Q_d(g)\subseteq T_d(g)\), and the order-\(d\) preordering SOS lower bound is at least the corresponding quadratic-module bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allowing square-free products of constraints can only strengthen the SOS lower bound at a common order.
assumptions_latex: The same generators and degree convention define \(Q_d(g)\) and \(T_d(g)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_d(g)\subseteq T_d(g)\) and \(\rho_d^{\mathrm{pre}}\geq\rho_d^{\mathrm{qm}}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Preordering Dominates the Quadratic Module

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Square-Free Product Count in a Preordering Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation-size consequence of assigning an SOS multiplier to every retained square-free product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(m\) inequality generators, a direct Gram representation of \(T_d(g)=\sum_{
u\in\{0,1\}^m}\Sigma[x]_{d_
u}g^
u\) uses at most \(2^m\) positive-semidefinite SOS blocks. It uses exactly \(2^m\) separately parameterized blocks when every square-free product \(g^
u\) fits the order-\(d\) truncation and none is omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direct preordering relaxation can use exponentially many SOS blocks in the number of inequality generators.
assumptions_latex: Each retained square-free product is assigned a separate SOS multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{SOS}}(d)\le2^m.

notation.meaning: Number of SOS multiplier blocks in the direct order- formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Square-Free Product Count in a Preordering Relaxation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Real-Radical Equalities Alone Do Not Ensure Preordering Saturation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample to saturation based only on a real-radical equality ideal and finiteness of the inequality-cut feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let I=(0)\subset\mathbb R[x] and let the sole inequality generator be g(x)=-x^2. Then I is real radical and K=\{x:-x^2\geq0\}=\{0\}. Nevertheless, p(x)=x is nonnegative on K and p\notin T(g)=\Sigma[x]-x^2\Sigma[x].
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even with a real-radical equality ideal and a singleton feasible set, a degenerate inequality presentation can yield a preordering that does not contain every polynomial nonnegative on the set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K=\{0\},\quad x\geq0\text{ on }K,\quad x\notin\Sigma[x]-x^2\Sigma[x].
knowledge_statements.title: Real-Radical Equalities Alone Do Not Ensure Preordering Saturation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonreduced Equality Ideals Can Obstruct Finite-Set Saturation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic boundary showing failure of SOS saturation modulo a non-real-radical equality ideal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K=\{x\in\mathbb R:x^2=0\}=\{0\} and let p(x)=x. Then p\geq0 on K, but p\notin (x^2)+\Sigma[x].
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the nonreduced singleton presentation x²=0, the polynomial x is nonnegative on the feasible set but is not SOS modulo (x²).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\geq0\text{ on }K,\qquad x\notin(x^2)+\Sigma[x].

notation.meaning: Cone of sums of squares in \(\mathbb R[x]\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nonreduced Equality Ideals Can Obstruct Finite-Set Saturation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Certificate and Atomic Moment Endpoint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite SOS exactness and attainment by an atomic moment sequence under support-ideal capture.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under finite-set support-ideal capture, let f^*=\min_K f. Then f-f^*\in I(h)+T(g), hence f-f^*\in I_{2d}(h)+T_d(g) for some d. At every order containing this identity, the preordering SOS bound equals f^*. For any minimizer u\in K, the truncated Dirac sequence y_\alpha=u^\alpha is feasible for the paired moment relaxation and attains f^*.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support-ideal capture gives a finite optimality certificate, and a Dirac measure at a minimizer attains the paired moment endpoint.
assumptions_latex: The paired order-d formulations contain every term of the certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max\{\gamma:f-\gamma\in I_{2d}(h)+T_d(g)\}=f^*=\min\{L_y(f):y\text{ is paired-moment feasible}\}.

notation.meaning: Truncated moments of the Dirac measure at u.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Certificate and Atomic Moment Endpoint

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient saturation condition for a preordering on a finite mixed feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K=\{x:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\ge0\} be finite and nonempty, let I(K)=\{p:p|_K=0\}, and suppose I(K)\subseteq I(h)+T(g). Then every polynomial p nonnegative on K belongs to I(h)+T(g).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the ideal-plus-preordering cone contains the vanishing ideal of the finite feasible set, it contains every polynomial nonnegative on that set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\in I(h)+T(g).

notation.meaning: Preordering generated by the inequality polynomials.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Set Saturation Under Support-Ideal Capture
Finite-Set Preordering Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preordering certificate allowing products of inequalities on a finite feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allowing square-free products of inequality generators yields a stronger finite-degree certificate; membership of the objective gap makes the finite-set relaxation exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed preordering identity certifies global optimality and makes the order-\(d\) preordering bound equal \(f_{\min}\).

notation.meaning: degree-truncated preordering generated by the inequalities
square-free product of inequality generators selected by ν

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the preordering-refinement leaf. Membership in the displayed preordering gives a valid nonnegativity certificate, but the exact relaxation and dual-attainment conclusions require a cited finite-order conic formulation and regularity theorem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Set Saturation of a Real-Reduced Preordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed saturation theorem for a finite mixed feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let I=\langle h\rangle\subset\mathbb R[x] be real radical, let T(g) be the preordering generated by g modulo I, and suppose K=\{h=0,\ g\geq0\} is finite and nonempty. The proposed claim is that every p\geq0 on K belongs to I+T(g).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed claim says that real radicality of the equality ideal and finiteness of the mixed feasible set force preordering saturation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\geq0\text{ on }K\Longrightarrow p\in I+T(g).

notation.meaning: Preordering generated by the inequality polynomials.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Set Saturation of a Real-Reduced Preordering

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible, Descent, and Feasible Descent Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions at a feasible point of a constrained optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let x^\star be feasible. A vector d\in\mathbb{R}^n is a feasible direction at x^\star if there exists \epsilon>0 such that x^\star+td is feasible for every t\in[0,\epsilon]. It is a descent direction if there exists \epsilon>0 such that f(x^\star+td)<f(x^\star) for every t\in[0,\epsilon]. It is a feasible descent direction if both properties hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible point, a direction is feasible when a sufficiently short forward segment remains feasible, is descending when the objective strictly decreases along such a segment, and is a feasible descent direction when both conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d\text{ is a feasible descent direction}\iff d\text{ is both feasible and descending at }x^\star.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Higher-order directional regularity for an operator between Banach spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An operator \(F:X\to Y\) is \(p\)-regular at \(x_*\) in the direction of \(H_{p-1}\in X^{p-1}\) if: (i) \(F\) is \((2p-1)\)-times continuously Fréchet differentiable near \(x_*\); (ii) the subspaces \(Y_i\), \(i=1,\ldots,p\), are closed; and (iii) \(\mathcal G_p[F](x_*;H_{p-1}):X\to Y_1\times(Y_2/Y_1)\times\cdots\times(Y/Y_{p-1})\), defined by \(v\mapsto(G_1(v),\ldots,\pi_{p-1}G_p(v))\), is onto.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An operator is directionally p-regular when it has continuous derivatives through order 2p−1, the associated subspaces are closed, and its p-factor operator onto the product of quotient spaces is surjective. For p=1 this recovers the classical Lyusternik condition.
assumptions_latex: F:X\to Y\text{ is an operator between Banach spaces}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is }p\text{-regular at }x_*\text{ along }H_{p-1}\iff\bigl[F\in C^{2p-1}\text{ near }x_*;\ Y_i\text{ are closed};\ \mathcal G_p[F](x_*;H_{p-1})\text{ is onto}\bigr].

children.title: Constraint-Qualification Regime
children.top_down_role: Active-constraint regularity at global minimizers.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Presentation dependence of LICQ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The equalities h_1(x)=x=0\text{ and }h_2(x)=2x=0\text{ define }K=\{0\},\text{ but }\nabla h_1(0)=1\text{ and }\nabla h_2(0)=2\text{ are dependent. Removing either redundant equality restores LICQ without changing }K.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A redundant displayed constraint can destroy LICQ without changing the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: LICQ uses every displayed equality and active inequality gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V_{\mathbb R}(h_1,h_2)=\{0\},\qquad \operatorname{rank}[\nabla h_1(0)\ \nabla h_2(0)]=1<2.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Constraints Can Destroy LICQ

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local KKT consequence of active-gradient independence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If x^* satisfies KKT stationarity and the equality gradients together with the active-inequality gradients are linearly independent, then the KKT multiplier vector is unique. LICQ alone neither proves optimality nor supplies a finite SOS certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional on KKT existence, LICQ makes the multipliers unique but is not an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\lambda,\mu_J)\text{ satisfying stationarity is unique}.
knowledge_statements.title: LICQ Multiplier Uniqueness
Constraint-Qualification Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-independence constraint qualification imposed at every global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(h_i(x)=0\) and \(g_j(x)\ge0\), with all polynomials continuously differentiable. For a feasible point \(x^*\), let \(J(x^*)=\{j:g_j(x^*)=0\}\). The constraint-qualification regime holds at \(x^*\) when \[\{\nabla h_i(x^*):1\le i\le m\}\cup\{\nabla g_j(x^*):j\in J(x^*)\}\] is linearly independent. Requiring this condition at every global minimizer ensures existence and uniqueness of the associated first-order multiplier vector whenever the stationarity equations are consistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each global minimizer, the equality gradients together with gradients of active inequalities must be linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The active constraint gradients are linearly independent at every global minimizer in this regime.

notation.meaning: index set of inequalities active at the feasible point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the constraint-qualification leaf, and the displayed condition is LICQ. An authoritative source is required for its use in this polynomial-optimization exactness context and for the multiplier existence-and-uniqueness statement, whose existence component additionally depends on KKT applicability or the stated consistency qualification.

children.title: Strict-Complementarity Regime
children.top_down_role: Multiplier regularity at active boundaries of global minimizers.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnecessity of strict complementarity for finite SOS certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \min\{x^2:x\ge0\}\text{ with }g(x)=x,\text{ the minimizer is }x^*=0.\text{ Stationarity }\nabla f(0)=\mu\nabla g(0)\text{ forces }\mu=0,\text{ so strict complementarity fails, while }f-f^*=x^2\in\Sigma[x].
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active inequality can have zero multiplier even though the problem has an immediate finite SOS certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g(0)=0,\qquad \mu=0,\qquad f-f^*=x^2\in\Sigma[x].
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Exactness Without Strict Complementarity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier quantification when active gradients are independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a KKT point x^* satisfying LICQ, the multiplier vector is unique. Therefore strict complementarity is equivalent to positivity of the unique multiplier for every active inequality. Without uniqueness, strict complementarity must specify existence of a KKT multiplier vector whose active components are all positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ removes multiplier ambiguity from strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{SC}(x^*)\Longleftrightarrow \mu_j>0\quad\forall j\in J(x^*)\text{ for the unique KKT multiplier}.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Complementarity Under LICQ
Strict-Complementarity Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive KKT multipliers for every inequality active at a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(h_i(x)=0\) and \(g_j(x)\ge0\), let \(x^*\) be a global minimizer satisfying KKT stationarity with multipliers \(\lambda_i\in\mathbb R\) and \(\mu_j\ge0\): \[
abla f(x^*)=\sum_i\lambda_i
abla h_i(x^*)+\sum_j\mu_j
abla g_j(x^*),\qquad \mu_jg_j(x^*)=0.\] Strict complementarity holds at \(x^*\) when \(\mu_j>0\) for every active inequality \(j\in J(x^*)\); equivalently, each inequality satisfies \(g_j(x^*)>0\) or \(\mu_j>0\). The regime requires this at every global minimizer.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let x^* be a local minimizer of the QQP and let (x^*,\mu^*) be a KKT pair satisfying strict complementarity, \mu_i^*>0 for every i\in\mathcal A(x^*). The modified second-order condition holds if any one of the following is true: (i) y^T\nabla^2q_0(x)y\ge0 for all y in the tangent space \mathcal T; (ii) all constraints are linear and x^* satisfies the stated second-order optimality condition; or (iii) all constraints are linear and the active gradients \{\nabla q_i(x^*):i\in\mathcal A(x^*)\} are linearly independent.

children.title: Boundary-Hessian Bridge
children.top_down_role: Interface between nonlinear-programming regularity and local algebraic certificate membership.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: NLP Regularity Implies the Boundary-Hessian Condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local conversion from nonlinear-programming regularity to boundary-adapted algebraic growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a global minimizer u, suppose the active-constraint gradients are linearly independent, all active inequality KKT multipliers are positive, and the Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite on the active tangent space. Then the active inequalities extend to regular local parameters in which f-f^* has positive linear coefficients in the active inward coordinates and a positive-definite quadratic part in the remaining tangent coordinates; hence the boundary-Hessian condition holds at u.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ, strict complementarity, and tangent-space second-order sufficiency imply the boundary-Hessian condition locally.
assumptions_latex: u is a KKT global minimizer.
The Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite on the active tangent space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{LICQ}+\operatorname{SC}+\operatorname{SOSC}\Longrightarrow\operatorname{BHC}\text{ at }u.
review_flags: Authoritative theorem locator desirable for the local-coordinate implication.
knowledge_statements.title: NLP Regularity Implies the Boundary-Hessian Condition
Boundary-Hessian Bridge
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Archimedean quadratic-module version of the boundary Hessian criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(Q(g)\) be Archimedean, and let \(f^*=\min_K f\). Suppose every zero \(u\in K\) of \(f-f^*\) is nonsingular on its active constraint variety and admits local parameters \(t_1,\ldots,t_n\), with the first \(k\) parameters equal to active constraints, such that the linear part of \(f-f^*\) has strictly positive coefficients in \(t_1,\ldots,t_k\) and its quadratic part in \(t_{k+1},\ldots,t_n\) is positive definite. Then \(f-f^*\in Q(g)\), so the associated sums-of-squares hierarchy is exact at some finite order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Archimedeanness and the boundary Hessian condition at every minimizer, the optimality gap belongs to the quadratic module and admits a finite-degree certificate.
assumptions_latex: The stated boundary Hessian condition holds at every global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f-f^*\in Q(g)\), hence \(f-f^*\in Q_d(g)\) for some finite \(d\).

children.title: Gradient-Ideal Regime
children.top_down_role: Critical-point ideal structure for unconstrained or equality-reduced polynomial optimization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical domain of a certificate modulo the gradient ideal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f-\gamma=\sigma+r\) with \(\sigma\in\Sigma[x]\) and \(r\in I_\nabla(f)\), then \(f(x)\ge\gamma\) for every \(x\in V_{\mathbb R}(I_\nabla(f))\). The identity alone does not establish the inequality at arbitrary noncritical points. It identifies the unconstrained optimum when an attained global minimizer is critical and \(\gamma\) is the minimum critical value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SOS modulo the gradient ideal certifies a bound on the real critical locus, not pointwise on all of Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in V_{\mathbb R}(I_\nabla(f))\Longrightarrow f(x)\ge\gamma.
knowledge_statements.title: Critical-Locus Versus Global-Domain Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact quotient certificate on a finite real critical locus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=V_{\mathbb R}(I_\nabla(f))\) be finite and \(m=\min_{x\in C}f(x)\). There is a polynomial \(s\) whose value at each \(u\in C\) is \(\sqrt{f(u)-m}\); hence \(f-m-s^2\in I(C)\) and \(f-m\in\Sigma[x]+I(C)\). If \(I_\nabla(f)=I(C)\), the certificate holds modulo the gradient ideal itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite real critical set, the critical-value gap is a square modulo its vanishing ideal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f-m\in\Sigma[x]+I(C),\qquad I_\nabla(f)=I(C)\Longrightarrow f-m\in\Sigma[x]+I_\nabla(f).

notation.meaning: Real vanishing ideal of the critical set.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Critical-Set SOS Representation
Gradient-Ideal Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained polynomial optimization with criticality imposed through the gradient ideal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), define the gradient ideal by \(I_\nabla(f)=\langle \partial f/\partial x_1,\ldots,\partial f/\partial x_n\rangle\). The gradient-ideal certificate regime holds when the global minimum \(f^*\) is attained and there exist a sum-of-squares polynomial \(\sigma\) and polynomials \(q_1,\ldots,q_n\) satisfying \[f-f^*=\sigma+\sum_{i=1}^n q_i\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}.\] Such an identity certifies \(f(x)\ge f^*\) at every real critical point; if every global minimizer is critical, it certifies the attained optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimality gap is represented by a sum of squares modulo the ideal generated by the objective’s partial derivatives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f-f^*\in \Sigma[x]+I_\nabla(f)\).

notation.meaning: Ideal generated by all partial derivatives of the objective.

review_flags: A source is needed for the intended finite-exactness version and any radicality or zero-dimensionality hypotheses.

The identity only establishes nonnegativity on the real critical locus, not on all of Euclidean space.

children.title: KKT-Ideal Regime
children.top_down_role: Multiplier-augmented equality structure for constrained polynomial optimization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition required for KKT augmentation to preserve the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A KKT augmentation preserves a global minimizer \(x^*\) only if \(x^*\) admits multipliers satisfying stationarity, complementarity, and the chosen signs. A constraint qualification at every global minimizer is sufficient for this lifting property. Without a KKT lift, restriction to the projected KKT set may exclude the true optimum; Fritz John criticality is the qualification-free first-order alternative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KKT augmentation is value-preserving only when at least one global minimizer, and for full optimizer coverage every global minimizer, has a KKT lift.
assumptions_latex: The original polynomial program attains its minimum.
The augmentation restricts optimization to the projected lifted KKT set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}f\cap\operatorname{proj}_xS_{\mathrm{KKT}}\ne\varnothing\text{ is required for value preservation}.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Qualification Coverage Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign-correct lifted set supporting ideal-plus-module certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(I_{\mathrm{KKT}}\subset\mathbb R[x,\lambda,\mu]\), define \[S_{\mathrm{KKT}}=\{(x,\lambda,\mu):p=0\ (p\in I_{\mathrm{KKT}}),\ g_j(x)\ge0,\ \mu_j\ge0\ \forall j\}.\] An identity \(f(x)-\gamma\in I_{\mathrm{KKT}}+Q(g,\mu)\), where \(Q(g,\mu)\) is the quadratic module generated by the lifted inequalities, certifies \(f(x)\ge\gamma\) on \(\operatorname{proj}_xS_{\mathrm{KKT}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KKT equations must be combined with primal and multiplier inequalities before ideal-module certification is valid.
assumptions_latex: The KKT ideal includes equality feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f-\gamma\in I_{\mathrm{KKT}}+Q(g,\mu)\Longrightarrow f(x)\ge\gamma\quad((x,\lambda,\mu)\in S_{\mathrm{KKT}}).

notation.meaning: Quadratic module generated by primal and multiplier inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted KKT Semialgebraic Set
KKT-Ideal Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-augmented polynomial ideal for equality and inequality constrained criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(h_i(x)=0\) and \(g_j(x)\ge0\), introduce multipliers \(\lambda_i\) and \(\mu_j\). The KKT ideal in \(\mathbb R[x,\lambda,\mu]\) is generated by \[h_i(x),\qquad \mu_jg_j(x),\qquad 
abla f(x)-\sum_i\lambda_i
abla h_i(x)-\sum_j\mu_j
abla g_j(x).\] The KKT-ideal regime requires every global minimizer to lift to a real zero of this ideal with \(\mu_j\ge0\). A sums-of-squares identity modulo the ideal, with inequality terms as needed, then yields a polynomial certificate on the lifted KKT set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KKT stationarity, feasibility, and complementarity are encoded as polynomial equations after adjoining multipliers, provided every minimizer has a nonnegative-multiplier lift.
assumptions_latex: Every global minimizer satisfies a constraint qualification ensuring KKT multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every global minimizer projects from the real KKT variety defined by \(I_{\mathrm{KKT}}\).

notation.meaning: Ideal generated by KKT stationarity, equality feasibility, and complementarity equations.

children.title: Fritz John-Ideal Regime
children.top_down_role: Criticality augmentation that does not presuppose standard constraint qualification.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary distinguishing qualification-free Fritz John criticality from KKT criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On the normalized Fritz John locus with \(\lambda_0=0\), stationarity is a nontrivial linear dependence among equality gradients and gradients of active inequalities. Such a tuple cannot be dehomogenized to KKT multipliers. A constraint qualification at a minimizer may ensure that a normal tuple with \(\lambda_0>0\) also exists, without eliminating abnormal components elsewhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An abnormal Fritz John tuple has zero objective multiplier and cannot be rescaled into a KKT tuple.
assumptions_latex: The multiplier tuple is nonzero through homogeneous normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_0=0\Longrightarrow\text{KKT dehomogenization is unavailable}.
knowledge_statements.title: Abnormal Fritz John Stratum

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normal Fritz John Points Reduce to KKT Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dehomogenization of the normal Fritz John stratum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a Fritz John tuple has \(\lambda_0>0\), division by \(\lambda_0\) produces KKT multipliers \(\widehat\lambda_i=\lambda_i/\lambda_0\) and \(\widehat\mu_j=\mu_j/\lambda_0\). Conversely, every KKT tuple gives a normal Fritz John tuple, unique only up to positive common scaling before normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive-objective-multiplier Fritz John stratum is the KKT system up to scaling.
assumptions_latex: The Fritz John and KKT systems use identical stationarity and sign conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x,\lambda_0,\lambda,\mu)\mapsto(x,\lambda/\lambda_0,\mu/\lambda_0)\text{ is a KKT lift}.
knowledge_statements.title: Normal Fritz John Points Reduce to KKT Points
Fritz John-Ideal Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous multiplier formulation that remains available without constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(h_i(x)=0\) and \(g_j(x)\ge0\), introduce \(\lambda_0,\lambda_i,\mu_j\). A normalized Fritz John ideal is generated by \[h_i(x),\quad \mu_jg_j(x),\quad \lambda_0
abla f(x)-\sum_i\lambda_i
abla h_i(x)-\sum_j\mu_j
abla g_j(x),\quad \lambda_0^2+\sum_i\lambda_i^2+\sum_j\mu_j^2-1.\] Every local minimizer has a lift satisfying these equations and appropriate multiplier signs, even when \(\lambda_0=0\). The regime is useful only after abnormal and spurious components are retained or separately excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fritz John equations encode constrained criticality using a possibly zero objective multiplier, avoiding reliance on a constraint qualification.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is defined by \(h_i=0\) and \(g_j\ge0\).
Multipliers are normalized and inequality multipliers have the chosen nonnegative sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every local minimizer lifts to the real normalized Fritz John variety, possibly with \(\lambda_0=0\).

notation.meaning: Fritz John multiplier of the objective gradient.

review_flags: A source is needed for the exact normalized ideal and multiplier-sign encoding used by the hierarchy.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Fritz John condition fits the container and correctly allows an abnormal objective multiplier, but the normalized ideal, multiplier signs, and handling of abnormal or spurious components require an exact source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spurious projections caused by omitted sign inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Stationarity, equality-feasibility, and complementarity equations alone do not enforce \(g_j(x)\ge0\) or \(\mu_j\ge0\). Their real variety may therefore project to primal-infeasible points or contain wrong-sign multiplier tuples. The intended critical set is obtained by intersecting with the required semialgebraic inequalities. Algebraic saturation can remove only components justified by its chosen nonvanishing conditions and cannot generally encode order signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equation-only KKT or Fritz John variety can contain spurious points because feasibility and multiplier signs are inequalities.
assumptions_latex: At least one required primal or multiplier sign inequality is omitted from the lifted set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_xV_{\mathbb R}(I)\text{ need not equal the feasible critical set}.
knowledge_statements.title: Equation-Only Multiplier Projection Boundary
Singular Optimality-Ideal Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic failure modes of gradient, KKT, and Fritz John ideals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be an optimality ideal used to augment a polynomial relaxation. If \(I\) is nonradical, its quotient algebra retains nilpotent multiplicity; if \(\dim V_{\mathbb C}(I)>0\), critical points cannot be isolated through a finite quotient basis; and if \(V_{\mathbb R}(I)\) contains components not projecting to feasible critical points, certificates on the augmented variety may address spurious points. These conditions invalidate arguments requiring a radical zero-dimensional ideal with an exact feasible projection. They do not, by themselves, prove that finite exactness is impossible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplicity, positive-dimensional critical varieties, or spurious components break standard zero-dimensional optimality-ideal arguments but do not alone rule out finite exactness.
assumptions_latex: The intended proof uses the complex or real variety of \(I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(I\) is nonradical, \(\dim V_{\mathbb C}(I)>0\), or its real projection is spurious, radical zero-dimensional certificate arguments do not apply.

notation.meaning: Complex affine variety of the ideal.
Krull dimension of the complex variety.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and qualified conclusion fit the node. However, no source connects nonradicality, positive dimension, and spurious projections to the particular optimality-ideal certificate arguments being delimited.

children.title: Generic Optimality Regularity
children.top_down_role: Generic-data regimes in which the relevant local optimality properties hold.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generic Regularity Is Not an Instance Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary of generic optimality assertions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A property holding on a nonempty Zariski-open U\subseteq P\text{ is not established for specified data }a\in P\text{ until }a\in U\text{ is verified. Moreover, local regularity alone does not imply finite SOS exactness without the other hypotheses of the applicable exactness theorem.}
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generic regularity neither certifies a specified instance nor replaces global exactness assumptions.
assumptions_latex: P is a coefficient parameter space.
U is a regular Zariski-open locus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a\in P\not\Rightarrow a\in U,\qquad a\in U\not\Rightarrow\text{ finite exactness without the remaining hypotheses}.
knowledge_statements.title: Generic Regularity Is Not an Instance Certificate
Generic Optimality Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zariski-generic regularity for fixed polynomial supports and constraint pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix degrees or monomial supports for \(f,h_i,g_j\), and regard their coefficients as a finite-dimensional parameter \(a\). When the relevant discriminant and resultant polynomials are not identically zero, their simultaneous nonvanishing defines a nonempty Zariski-open set \(U\). For \(a\in U\), feasible critical points are nonsingular and isolated; at local minimizers, constraint qualification, strict complementarity, and second-order nondegeneracy hold whenever the corresponding defining resultants are included. Thus the exceptional parameters lie in a proper real algebraic subset and have Lebesgue measure zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For fixed supports, nonvanishing discriminants and resultants define a Zariski-open coefficient set where the encoded optimality systems are regular and isolated.
assumptions_latex: Coefficient parameters range over a finite-dimensional real affine space \(P\).
The relevant discriminant and resultant polynomials are not identically zero.
The chosen algebraic tests encode all asserted regularity properties.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists a nonempty Zariski-open \(U\subseteq P\) on which the encoded optimality regularity holds; \(P\setminus U\) is algebraic and null.

notation.meaning: Coefficient parameter space for the fixed polynomial supports.

review_flags: The exact genericity theorem and its degree or support hypotheses require an authoritative source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the generic-regularity container, but the asserted simultaneous generic constraint qualification, strict complementarity, isolatedness, and second-order nondegeneracy depends on specifically constructed discriminants or resultants that are neither defined nor cited.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generic Constraint Qualification, Strict Complementarity, and Second-Order Sufficiency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient-space generic regularity for fixed-degree polynomial optimization data at every local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(d_0,\ldots,d_{m_1},d'_1,\ldots,d'_{m_2}\in\mathbb N\), and consider \(P:\inf\{f(\mathbf x):\mathbf x\in K\}\) with \(K\) as in (7.2). There exist finitely many real polynomials \(\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_L\) in the coefficients of \((f,g_1,\ldots,g_{m_1},h_1,\ldots,h_{m_2})\) such that, if \(\varphi_i\ne0\) at the input data for every \(i=1,\ldots,L\), then constraint qualification (7.4), strict complementarity, and the second-order sufficient condition (7.7) hold at every local minimizer \(\mathbf x^*\in K\) of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For fixed polynomial degrees, there are finitely many coefficient polynomials whose simultaneous nonvanishing guarantees constraint qualification, strict complementarity, and second-order sufficiency at every local minimizer. Thus failures are confined to the union of their coefficient-space zero sets.
assumptions_latex: P=\inf\{f(\mathbf x):\mathbf x\in K\},\quad K\text{ is as in (7.2)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\,\mathbf x^*\in K\text{ that are local minimizers of }P,\quad \mathrm{QC}(\mathbf x^*)\wedge\mathrm{SC}(\mathbf x^*)\wedge\mathrm{SOSC}(\mathbf x^*)

source_evidence.locator: Global optimality certificates / 7.1. Putinar versus Karush-Kuhn-Tucker / Theorem 7.6
