children.title: Discriminantal Exceptional Sets
children.top_down_role: Algebraic parameter loci associated with singularity, multiplicity, or loss of regularity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Properness Boundary for a Discriminantal Locus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates algebraicity from genuine exceptionality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let E\subseteq P\text{ be the Zariski closure of parameters for which a specified polynomial system has a relevant singular solution. Algebraicity permits }E=P.\text{ Properness requires a parameter outside }E,\text{ equivalently a nonzero parameter polynomial vanishing on }E.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An elimination-defined singular locus need not be a proper exceptional set; it may fill parameter space.
assumptions_latex: The singularity incidence set and its parameter closure are algebraic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E\subsetneq P\text{ requires an independent properness witness; }E=P\text{ is possible}.
knowledge_statements.title: Properness Boundary for a Discriminantal Locus
Discriminantal Exceptional Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic coefficient loci where an encoded optimality system loses regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(z;a)=(F_1(z;a),\ldots,F_r(z;a))\) be a polynomial optimality system with coefficient parameter \(a\in P\). Its singular exceptional set is the Zariski closure \[E=\overline{\{a\in P:\exists z\in\mathbb C^N,\ F(z;a)=0,\ \operatorname{rank}D_zF(z;a)<r\}}^{\,Z}.\] Eliminating \(z\) from the equations \(F(z;a)=0\) and the maximal minors of \(D_zF(z;a)\) produces equations for \(E\). Additional elimination conditions may be adjoined to record multiplicity, roots at infinity, or failure of a constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exceptional locus is the algebraic closure of coefficient values for which the polynomial optimality system has a singular solution.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is polynomial in variables \(z\) and parameters \(a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E\subseteq P\) is Zariski closed and is computable by elimination from the singularity equations.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the optimality system with respect to its variables.

review_flags: A source is needed for the precise discriminant construction used for polynomial optimality systems.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the exceptional-set container, but rank loss below r is not a generally valid singularity test for an arbitrary r-equation system without dimensional or complete-intersection hypotheses. The precise elimination and saturation construction needs a source.

children.title: Nongeneric Finite Exactness
children.top_down_role: Special exact instances not explained by generic optimality regularity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of second-order nondegeneracy without failure of finite SOS exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \min_{x\in\mathbb R}x^4,\quad x^*=0,\quad f^*=0,\quad f''(0)=0,\quad f-f^*=x^4=(x^2)^2\in\Sigma[x]_4.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quartic has a degenerate minimizer but an immediate finite SOS certificate.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation order contains degree four.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Second-order nondegeneracy fails, while finite SOS exactness holds.}

notation.meaning: SOS polynomials of degree at most four.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate but Finitely Exact Quartic
Nongeneric Finite Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instance-specific finite certificates on an exceptional coefficient locus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x:h_i(x)=0,\ g_j(x)\ge0\}\), let \(f^*=\min_K f\), and define the truncated certificate cone \(C_d=I_{2d}(h)+Q_d(g)\). An exceptional or nongeneric instance is finitely exact whenever there exists a finite \(d\) and polynomials \(p_i\), sums of squares \(\sigma_j\), satisfying the degree bounds of \(C_d\), such that \[f-f^*=\sum_i p_i h_i+\sigma_0+\sum_j\sigma_jg_j.\] This identity certifies the optimum independently of generic constraint qualification, strict complementarity, or isolatedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even nongeneric data are finitely exact when the optimality gap has a finite-degree ideal-plus-quadratic-module representation.
assumptions_latex: The displayed identity respects the truncation degree \(2d\).
Each \(\sigma_j\) is a sum of squares.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f-f^*\in C_d\) for some finite \(d\), so the order-\(d\) relaxation is exact.
review_flags: A hierarchy-specific source is needed for the truncation convention and exactness equivalence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the node and the displayed membership is an instance-specific finite certificate, but the truncation convention and equivalence with exactness of the stated relaxation require a hierarchy-specific citation.

children.title: Finite-Exactness Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where asymptotic certificate validity need not imply exactness at a finite order.

children.title: Positive-Dimensional Minimizer Sets
children.top_down_role: Continua of global minimizers and their finite-exactness complications.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Continuum of Minimizers Can Have Immediate SOS Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that positive-dimensional minimizer geometry is not itself an obstruction to finite exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:1-x^2-y^2\geq0\}\) and \(f(x,y)=x^2\). Then \(f^*=0\), \(\operatorname{argmin}_K f=\{(0,y):-1\leq y\leq1\}\) is one-dimensional, and \(f-f^*=x^2\) is a sum of squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the unit disk, x² has a diameter of minimizers but an immediate SOS certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim\operatorname{argmin}_K f=1\) and \(f-f^*=x^2\in\Sigma[x,y]\).
knowledge_statements.title: A Continuum of Minimizers Can Have Immediate SOS Exactness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Flat Atomic Extraction Cannot Enumerate a Minimizer Continuum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits support recovery when the full minimizer set is positive-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the global minimizer set \(M\) is positive-dimensional, a flat moment certificate yields only a finitely supported representing measure. It can certify each recovered atom as a minimizer, but its finite support cannot equal the entire continuum \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite atomic extraction can recover selected minimizers from a continuum, not the entire minimizer set.
assumptions_latex: A flat moment certificate yields a finitely atomic representing measure \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{supp}\mu\subseteq M\) is finite and \(\operatorname{supp}\mu\neq M\).

notation.meaning: finitely atomic representing measure extracted from a flat moment sequence

knowledge_statements.title: Flat Atomic Extraction Cannot Enumerate a Minimizer Continuum

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic dimension convention for continua of global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an attained polynomial optimization problem on a semialgebraic feasible set K, let M=\{x\in K:f(x)=f^*\}. The minimizer locus is positive-dimensional when its semialgebraic dimension satisfies \dim M\ge1. Equivalently, a semialgebraic stratification of M contains a positive-dimensional stratum, or M contains a nonconstant semialgebraic arc. This definition does not use the complex dimension of the Zariski closure of M.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimizer set is positive-dimensional when it has positive semialgebraic dimension, equivalently when it contains a positive-dimensional stratum or a nonconstant semialgebraic arc.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \dim M\ge1\iff M\text{ contains a positive-dimensional semialgebraic stratum}\iff M\text{ contains a nonconstant semialgebraic arc}.

notation.meaning: Semialgebraic dimension of the minimizer set.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Dimensional Semialgebraic Minimizer Locus
Positive-Dimensional Minimizer Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of isolated-minimizer arguments when the minimizing locus has positive dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=\{x\in K:f(x)=f^*\}\). If the real algebraic dimension of the Zariski closure of \(M\) is positive, then \(M\) is not a finite set of isolated points. Consequently, finite-exactness proofs based on a zero-dimensional minimizer ideal, finite interpolation over minimizers, or nonsingular isolated critical points are unavailable. Positive dimension is not itself an obstruction to a certificate: finite exactness still holds whenever \(f-f^*\) belongs to the relevant finite truncation of the equality ideal plus quadratic module.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuum of minimizers defeats isolated-point certificate arguments, although a separate finite polynomial identity may still establish exactness.
assumptions_latex: The Zariski closure of \(M\) has positive dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Zero-dimensional minimizer arguments fail, but positive dimension alone does not imply \(f-f^*\notin I_{2d}(h)+Q_d(g)\) for every \(d\).
review_flags: A source is needed for the precise finite-exactness implications of positive-dimensional minimizer varieties.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and cautious conclusion fit the container, but the phrase 'real algebraic dimension of the Zariski closure' is ambiguous and the claimed limits of the cited proof mechanisms need authoritative support.

children.title: Singular Minimizers
children.top_down_role: Global minimizers at singular points of the feasible geometry.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singularity Does Not Preclude Finite Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A singular constraint presentation with an immediate finite certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \min\{x^2:x^2=0\}\text{ has the singular minimizer }x^*=0,\text{ since }\nabla(x^2)(0)=0.\text{ Nevertheless }f-f^*=x^2=h\in I(h).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singularly presented minimizer can still have an immediate finite-degree ideal certificate.
assumptions_latex: The equality ideal is included in the certificate cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\text{ is singular for the displayed constraint, while }f-f^*\in I_2(h).
knowledge_statements.title: Singularity Does Not Preclude Finite Exactness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes singular constraint descriptions from intrinsic feasible-set singularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: K=\{0\}\subset\mathbb R\text{ is represented both by }h(x)=x=0\text{ and }\widetilde h(x)=x^2=0,\text{ but }\operatorname{rank}Dh(0)=1\text{ and }\operatorname{rank}D\widetilde h(0)=0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent polynomial descriptions can classify the same feasible point differently under a displayed-Jacobian rank test.
assumptions_latex: Singularity is evaluated from the displayed constraint gradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V_{\mathbb R}(h)=V_{\mathbb R}(\widetilde h)=\{0\},\qquad \operatorname{rank}Dh(0)\ne\operatorname{rank}D\widetilde h(0).
knowledge_statements.title: Presentation Dependence of Rank Singularity
Singular Minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimizers where the active feasible geometry has deficient Jacobian rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\{x:h_i(x)=0,\ g_j(x)\ge0\}\) and \(u\in K\), let \(A(u)=\{j:g_j(u)=0\}\). The minimizer \(u\) is singular when the gradients \(\{\nabla h_i(u)\}_i\cup\{\nabla g_j(u):j\in A(u)\}\) fail the rank condition required by the chosen constraint qualification. At such a point, KKT multipliers may fail to exist or may be nonunique, and regular local parameters need not exist. Therefore finite-exactness theorems requiring constraint qualification or a smooth active variety cannot be invoked at \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular minimizer has rank-deficient active constraints, so regular KKT and smooth-local-coordinate exactness theorems may not apply.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Rank deficiency at \(u\) blocks certificate theorems whose hypotheses require regular active constraints; it does not alone disprove finite exactness.

notation.meaning: Indices of inequality constraints active at the minimizer.

review_flags: A source is required for the exact singularity and constraint-qualification convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but singularity is defined relative to an unspecified rank condition and constraint qualification. The consequences for multiplier existence, uniqueness, and local parameters vary with that choice and require a precise source.

children.title: Degenerate Boundary Contact
children.top_down_role: Loss of boundary regularity at minimizing zeros.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary-Hessian Degeneracy Does Not Preclude Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that a zero boundary slope need not obstruct a finite SOS certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Minimize \(f(x)=x^2\) on \(K=[0,1]=\{x:x\geq0,\ 1-x\geq0\}\). At the minimizer \(u=0\), the active boundary coordinate \(t=x\) gives \(f-f(u)=t^2\), whose linear boundary coefficient is zero. Nevertheless \(f-f^*=x^2\) is a sum of squares, so an SOS relaxation containing degree two is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing x² on [0,1] has zero boundary slope at the minimizer but an immediate SOS certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The positive-boundary-slope condition fails at \(0\), yet \(f-f^*=x^2\in\Sigma[x]\).
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Hessian Degeneracy Does Not Preclude Exactness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of a Sufficient Boundary Criterion Is Inconclusive
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits conclusions drawn from loss of positive boundary slope or tangent curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a regular boundary minimizer, failure of a positive active linear coefficient or positive-definite tangent quadratic part prevents application of the boundary-Hessian finite-exactness theorem. It does not imply that \(f-f^*\) lies outside every finite certificate cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boundary degeneracy removes one sufficient theorem but does not prove nonexactness.
assumptions_latex: The boundary-Hessian theorem is used only as a sufficient condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of its hypotheses is not a converse certificate of nonexactness.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure of a Sufficient Boundary Criterion Is Inconclusive

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precise local expansion defining the boundary-contact failure regime without asserting an unconditional KKT equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let u be a regular boundary minimizer and choose regular local parameters t_1,\ldots,t_n so that the active inequalities are t_1,\ldots,t_k\ge0. Write the local expansion f-f(u)=f_1+f_2+\text{higher-order terms}, where f_j is homogeneous of degree j in the parameters. Boundary-Hessian nondegeneracy requires f_1=\sum_{i=1}^k a_i t_i with every a_i>0 and requires the restriction of f_2 to the tangent variables t_{k+1},\ldots,t_n to be positive definite. Degenerate boundary contact means that at least one of these requirements fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a regular boundary minimizer, boundary contact is nondegenerate when active boundary slopes are positive and tangent quadratic curvature is positive definite; failure of either condition is degenerate contact.
assumptions_latex: Regular local parameters adapted to the active inequalities exist at u.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Degenerate contact}\iff(\exists i\le k:a_i\le0)\ \lor\ \big(f_2|_{\operatorname{span}(t_{k+1},\ldots,t_n)}\text{ is not positive definite}\big).

notation.meaning: Local parameters corresponding to active inequalities.
Linear and quadratic homogeneous terms of the local objective-gap expansion.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Hessian Nondegeneracy and Degenerate Contact
Degenerate Boundary Contact
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of first- or second-order boundary nondegeneracy at a minimizing zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u\in K\) minimize \(f\), and suppose regular local parameters place the active inequalities in coordinates \(t_1,\ldots,t_k\). Boundary contact is degenerate if the expansion of \(f-f(u)\) has a nonpositive or zero coefficient in an active coordinate, or if its quadratic form in the remaining tangent coordinates is not positive definite. Equivalently, strict complementarity or second-order sufficiency fails in this local model. The boundary Hessian criterion then fails at \(u\), so the corresponding theorem cannot certify \(f-f^*\) in the quadratic module.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero boundary slope or a degenerate tangent Hessian violates the boundary Hessian criterion and removes its finite-certificate guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(u\) is a global minimizer on a basic closed semialgebraic set.
Regular local boundary coordinates exist at \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of a positive active linear coefficient or positive-definite tangent quadratic part prevents application of the boundary Hessian certificate theorem.

notation.meaning: Local coordinates corresponding to active inequalities.

review_flags: An authoritative locator for the boundary Hessian criterion and its failure conditions is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the node, but equivalence between boundary-Hessian failure and failure of strict complementarity or second-order sufficiency requires explicit regularity hypotheses and a cited theorem. The exact local expansion convention is also unsourced.

children.title: Asymptotic Without Finite Exactness
children.top_down_role: Hierarchy-valid regimes without a structural guarantee of exactness at any finite order.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates certificates for finite attainment from those yielding only asymptotic convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\rho_d=\sup\{\gamma:f-\gamma\in Q_d(g)\}\), feasibility of \(\gamma=f^*\) at order \(d\) is equivalent to \(f-f^*\in Q_d(g)\). In contrast, if \(f-f^*+\varepsilon\in Q(g)\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\), then sufficiently large truncations yield bounds arbitrarily close to \(f^*\), but this does not supply membership of the unperturbed gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite exactness needs an unperturbed finite-degree certificate; certificates for all positive perturbations give only limiting convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unperturbed finite membership certifies finite exactness, whereas membership of every positive perturbation yields only asymptotic approximation absent further information.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Exactness Versus Perturbed Membership

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Value Equality Need Not Supply an Attained Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates equality of a fixed-order supremum from feasibility of its endpoint certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a fixed order, \(\rho_d=f^*\) does not imply \(f-f^*\in Q_d(g)\) unless the SOS supremum is attained. A nonattained supremum can therefore equal the true optimum without producing an optimal certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-order SOS value can equal the optimum as a nonattained supremum.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_d\) is defined as a supremum of feasible certificate bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_d=f^*\not\Rightarrow f-f^*\in Q_d(g)\) without endpoint attainment.
knowledge_statements.title: Value Equality Need Not Supply an Attained Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Archimedean Perturbation Convergence Without Endpoint Membership
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Putinar-based mechanism producing asymptotic convergence while separating the unperturbed endpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0\}\ne\varnothing and suppose Q(g) is Archimedean. If f^*=\min_K f, then for every \varepsilon>0, Putinar's strict-positivity theorem gives f-f^*+\varepsilon\in Q(g). Therefore, for some d(\varepsilon), f-(f^*-\varepsilon)\in Q_{d(\varepsilon)}(g), and the increasing SOS bounds converge to f^*. This conclusion alone does not imply f-f^*\in Q(g) or exactness at a finite order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Archimedeanity certifies every positive perturbation of the optimality gap and hence convergence, but it does not certify the unperturbed gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\varepsilon>0\ \exists d(\varepsilon):\ f-f^*+\varepsilon\in Q_{d(\varepsilon)}(g),\quad \rho_d\uparrow f^*.

notation.meaning: Quadratic module generated by the inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Archimedean Perturbation Convergence Without Endpoint Membership

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Motzkin Optimality Gap Has No Finite Ball-Module Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit compact Archimedean problem whose nonnegative optimality gap is outside the full quadratic module although every positive perturbation is certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:1-x^2-y^2-z^2\ge0\}\), \(g=1-x^2-y^2-z^2\), and \[M=x^4y^2+x^2y^4+z^6-3x^2y^2z^2.\] Then \(M\ge0\) on \(\mathbb R^3\), \(\min_K M=0\), and the quadratic module \(Q(g)=\{\sigma_0+\sigma_1g:\sigma_0,\sigma_1\text{ are sums of squares}\}\) is Archimedean. Nevertheless, \(M\notin Q(g)\). Consequently no finite truncation contains the unperturbed optimality gap, whereas \(M+\varepsilon\in Q(g)\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the unit ball, the Motzkin form has minimum zero and every positive perturbation has an Archimedean certificate, but the exact optimality gap has no finite-degree quadratic-module certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_KM=0,\quad M\notin Q(g),\quad \forall\varepsilon>0:\ M+\varepsilon\in Q(g).\)

notation.meaning: Quadratic module generated by the unit-ball inequality.

review_flags: Endpoint nonmembership excludes a finite-degree optimal certificate but does not by itself prove that every fixed-order certificate supremum is attained or strictly below zero.
A source locator for the standard Motzkin non-SOS fact and the resulting ball-module nonmembership would strengthen the record.
knowledge_statements.title: Motzkin Optimality Gap Has No Finite Ball-Module Certificate
Asymptotic Without Finite Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Archimedean convergence when the unperturbed optimality gap lacks a finite certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0\}\) and suppose its quadratic module \(Q(g)\) is Archimedean. If \(f^*=\min_K f\), then for every \(\varepsilon>0\), strict positivity gives \(f-f^*+\varepsilon\in Q(g)\). Hence the lower bounds produced by the truncated quadratic-module hierarchy converge to \(f^*\). This does not imply \(f-f^*\in Q(g)\): when the unperturbed gap has no finite-degree representation, no relaxation order attains \(f^*\), despite asymptotic convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Archimedeanness certifies every positive perturbation of the optimality gap, yielding convergence without necessarily yielding exactness at any finite order.
assumptions_latex: The hierarchy uses increasing degree truncations \(Q_d(g)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f-f^*+\varepsilon\in Q(g)\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\), while finite exactness additionally requires \(f-f^*\in Q_d(g)\) for some \(d\).

notation.meaning: Archimedean quadratic module generated by the constraints.
Arbitrary positive perturbation of the optimality gap.

review_flags: A source is required for the strict-positivity Positivstellensatz and the stated hierarchy convergence implication.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and distinction between asymptotic convergence and finite membership are mathematically appropriate, but the Archimedean strict-positivity Positivstellensatz and hierarchy-convergence implication have no cited source or locator.

children.title: Coercive Objectives
children.top_down_role: Objective-growth regimes controlling escape along unbounded feasible directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Coercive Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coercivity relative to a possibly unbounded feasible set in Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and let \(f:K\to\mathbb R\). The objective \(f\) is coercive on \(K\) when every feasible sequence escaping to infinity has diverging objective values:
\[
(x_k\in K,\ \|x_k\|\to\infty)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad f(x_k)\to +\infty.
\]
Equivalently, for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), the sublevel set \(\{x\in K:f(x)\leq\alpha\}\) is bounded. If \(K\) is closed and \(f\) is lower semicontinuous, these sublevel sets are compact and every finite infimum of \(f\) on \(K\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coercive objective grows without bound along every unbounded feasible sequence; with closed feasibility and lower semicontinuity, it attains its minimum.
assumptions_latex: For the attainment conclusion, \(K\) is closed and \(f\) is lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x_k\|\to\infty\Rightarrow f(x_k)\to+\infty\), and under closedness and lower semicontinuity, \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}f(x)\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Feasible sublevel set at level alpha.

source_refs.locator: 2.1.1 Problem Statement and Basic Assumptions p. 41

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1.1 Problem Statement and Basic Assumptions p. 41

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial-specific sufficient condition for coercivity and its sharp logical boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) have even degree \(2d\) and leading homogeneous form \(p_{2d}\). If \(p_{2d}(u)>0\) for every \(u\neq0\), then \(p(x)\to+\infty\) as \(\|x\|\to\infty\). The converse fails: \(p(x,y)=x^2+y^4\) is coercive although its degree-four leading form \(y^4\) vanishes on nonzero vectors \((x,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite leading form guarantees polynomial coercivity, but coercive polynomials may have a degenerate highest-degree form.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is a real polynomial of even degree \(2d\).
For the sufficient implication, \(p_{2d}\) is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{2d}>0\text{ on }\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\Rightarrow p\text{ is coercive}\), but the converse is false.
knowledge_statements.title: Leading-Form Criterion and Its Nonconverse

children.title: Compact Sublevel Sets
children.top_down_role: Effective compactness restricted to optimization-relevant objective levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Compact Sublevel Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Level compactness sufficient for existence without requiring the entire feasible set to be compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed, and let \(f:K\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous. Suppose there exists \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\) such that \(L_\alpha:=\{x\in K:f(x)\leq\alpha\}\) is nonempty and compact. If \(\inf_{x\in K}f(x)<\alpha\), then every minimizing sequence is eventually confined to a compact sublevel \(L_\beta\subseteq L_\alpha\) for some \(\beta<\alpha\), and \(f\) attains its global infimum on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One nonempty compact sublevel strictly above the infimum confines minimizing sequences and guarantees attainment for a lower-semicontinuous objective.
assumptions_latex: \(L_\alpha\) is nonempty and compact with \(\inf_K f<\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}f(x)\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Feasible sublevel set at level alpha.
Global infimum of the objective over the feasible set.

source_refs.locator: 2.1.1 Problem Statement and Basic Assumptions p. 41

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of attainment despite a compact nonempty sublevel when lower semicontinuity is omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=[0,1]\), \(f(0)=1\), and \(f(x)=x\) for \(x\in(0,1]\). Then \(L_1=K\) is compact and \(\inf_K f=0<1\), but the infimum is not attained because \(f\) is not lower semicontinuous at \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact sublevel above the infimum does not guarantee attainment without lower semicontinuity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_1=K\text{ is compact},\ \inf_K f=0,\ \operatorname*{argmin}_K f=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Lower Semicontinuity Is Essential

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the unit sublevel set associated with a real multivariate polynomial; no compactness or other geometric regularity is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a polynomial $g\in\mathbb{R}[\mathbf{x}]$ in $n$ real variables, its unit sublevel set is defined by
\[
\mathbf{G}:=\{\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n:g(\mathbf{x})\le 1\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a real polynomial g in n variables, its unit sublevel set G consists of all points x in R^n for which g(x) is at most 1.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf{G}:=\{\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n:g(\mathbf{x})\le 1\}

children.title: Attained Noncoercive Regimes
children.top_down_role: Unbounded problems with attained optima despite failure of coercivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Attained Noncoercive Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment characterized independently of coercivity on an unbounded feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and unbounded, and let \(f:K\to\mathbb R\) have finite infimum \(f_*:=\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\). The problem is in an attained noncoercive regime precisely when
\[
\{x\in K:f(x)=f_*\}\neq\varnothing
\quad\text{and}\quad
\exists (x_k)\subseteq K:\ \|x_k\|\to\infty,\ \sup_k f(x_k)<+\infty.
\]
The first condition gives a global minimizer, while the second is equivalent to failure of coercivity on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum is achieved at a feasible point even though an unbounded feasible sequence has bounded objective values, so coercivity fails.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}f(x)\neq\varnothing\) while \(f\) is not coercive on \(K\).

notation.meaning: Infimum of the objective over the feasible set.

source_refs.locator: 2.1.1 Problem Statement and Basic Assumptions p. 41

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1.1 Problem Statement and Basic Assumptions p. 41

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary polynomial model separating existence of minimizers from coercive growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\mathbb R^2\) and \(f(x,y)=x^2\), \(\inf_K f=0\) and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_K f=\{0\}\times\mathbb R\). Nevertheless, \(f(0,k)=0\) while \(\|(0,k)\|\to\infty\), so \(f\) is not coercive on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polynomial x squared attains its minimum along an unbounded line although it is noncoercive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_K f=\{0\}\times\mathbb R\neq\varnothing\) and \(f\) is not coercive on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.title: Attainment Does Not Imply Coercivity

children.title: Nonattainment at Infinity
children.top_down_role: Infimal behavior escaping along unbounded feasible sequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonattainment at Infinity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite infimum approached only by feasible sequences escaping every bounded set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed, and let \(f:K\to\mathbb R\) have finite infimum \(f_*:=\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\). Nonattainment at infinity occurs when
\[
\{x\in K:f(x)=f_*\}=\varnothing
\]
and every minimizing sequence escapes every bounded set:
\[
\forall (x_k)\subseteq K,\qquad f(x_k)\to f_*\ \Longrightarrow\ \|x_k\|\to\infty.
\]
Consequently, for every \(\alpha>f_*\), the feasible sublevel set \(\{x\in K:f(x)\leq\alpha\}\) is unbounded, and evaluation at an affine global minimizer is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The finite infimum is not achieved, and every feasible sequence approaching it escapes to infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}f(x)=\varnothing\) and every minimizing sequence satisfies \(\|x_k\|\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: Finite global infimum over the feasible set.

source_refs.locator: 2.1.1 Problem Statement and Basic Assumptions p. 41

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1.1 Problem Statement and Basic Assumptions p. 41

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity condition under which finite nonattainment forces every minimizing sequence to escape.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed, and let \(f:K\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be lower semicontinuous with finite infimum \(f_*\). If \(\operatorname*{argmin}_K f=\varnothing\), then every sequence \((x_k)\subseteq K\) satisfying \(f(x_k)\to f_*\) obeys \(\|x_k\|\to\infty\). Closedness alone is insufficient without lower semicontinuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a lower-semicontinuous objective on a closed finite-dimensional feasible set, a nonattained finite infimum can only be approached at infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_k)\to f_*\Longrightarrow\|x_k\|\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Semicontinuity Boundary for Escape

children.title: Hilbert's Seventeenth-Problem Regime
children.top_down_role: Global nonnegativity setting permitting rational-function certificate structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Hilbert's Seventeenth-Problem Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Artin’s rational-sum-of-squares characterization of globally nonnegative real polynomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\). Then \(p(x)\geq0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) if and only if \(p\) is a sum of squares in the rational function field \(\mathbb R(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\):
\[
p=\sum_{i=1}^m r_i^2,
\qquad r_i\in\mathbb R(x_1,\ldots,x_n).
\]
Equivalently, there exist a nonzero polynomial \(q\in\mathbb R[x]\) and polynomials \(s_1,\ldots,s_m\in\mathbb R[x]\) such that \(q^2p=\sum_{i=1}^m s_i^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real polynomial is globally nonnegative exactly when it is a sum of squares of rational functions, equivalently after multiplication by a squared polynomial denominator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\geq0\text{ on }\mathbb R^n\iff p\in\sum\mathbb R(x_1,\ldots,x_n)^2\).

notation.meaning: Real polynomial ring in the stated variables.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Artin's rational-sum-of-squares theorem is stated correctly and theorem is the proper content kind, but no inspectable authoritative citation is supplied.

children.title: Uniform-Denominator Regime
children.top_down_role: Problem classes admitting denominators from controlled families.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform-Denominator Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A polynomial class sharing denominators from a prescribed controlled family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal P\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) be a class of globally nonnegative polynomials and let \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\setminus\{0\}\) be a prescribed denominator family. The pair \((\mathcal P,\mathcal D)\) has the uniform-denominator property when
\[
\forall p\in\mathcal P\ \exists q\in\mathcal D:\quad q^2p\in\Sigma[x],
\]
where \(\Sigma[x]\) is the cone of polynomial sums of squares. Uniformity refers to the common restriction \(q\in\mathcal D\); it does not require one fixed denominator for every \(p\) unless \(\mathcal D\) is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonnegative polynomial in the class becomes polynomial SOS after multiplication by a squared denominator chosen from one controlled family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall p\in\mathcal P\ \exists q\in\mathcal D:\ q^2p\in\Sigma[x]\).

notation.meaning: Cone of sums of squares of real polynomials.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is internally coherent, but the intended meaning of uniform denominator varies in the literature. A source must support this controlled-family quantifier structure.

children.title: Weighted SOS Regime
children.top_down_role: Growth-adapted weighted certificate systems on unbounded domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted SOS Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A prescribed weighted SOS cone encoding growth on an unbounded domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(w_0,\ldots,w_m\in\mathbb R[x]\) be fixed weights nonnegative on \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). The associated weighted sum-of-squares cone is
\[
M_w:=\left\{\sum_{j=0}^m w_j\sigma_j:\ \sigma_j\in\Sigma[x]\right\}.
\]
A polynomial family \(\mathcal P\) lies in the weighted SOS regime on \(K\) when every \(p\in\mathcal P\) that is strictly positive on \(K\), subject to the stipulated growth assumptions, belongs to \(M_w\). Membership supplies the identity \(p=\sum_jw_j\sigma_j\), which directly certifies \(p\geq0\) on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed nonnegative weights combine with SOS multipliers to represent positive polynomials whose growth matches the chosen certificate system.
assumptions_latex: Each fixed weight \(w_j\) is nonnegative on \(K\).
The polynomial family satisfies the growth hypotheses attached to the chosen weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=\sum_{j=0}^m w_j\sigma_j\) with \(\sigma_j\in\Sigma[x]\), hence \(p\geq0\) on \(K\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted cone is defined correctly, but the asserted positive-polynomial representation depends on unstated growth hypotheses and the chosen weight system. Its reliable mathematical version requires a source.

children.title: Constrained Denominator Regime
children.top_down_role: Denominator certificate assumptions adapted to noncompact semialgebraic sets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact preordering-multiplier characterization allowing zeros of the target on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With the same notation, \(f\geq0\) on \(K\) if and only if there exist an integer \(r\geq1\) and \(p,q\in T(g)\) such that \(pf=f^{2r}+q\). The multiplier need not be nonzero at feasible zeros of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible nonnegativity is characterized by a preordering-multiplier identity containing an even power of the target; feasible zeros prevent requiring a nonvanishing multiplier in general.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\geq0\text{ on }K\iff \exists r\geq1,\ p,q\in T(g):\ pf=f^{2r}+q\).

notation.meaning: positive integer exponent in the nonnegative Positivstellensatz

knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegative Krivine–Stengle Variant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact preordering-multiplier characterization of strict positivity on a basic closed semialgebraic set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_1(x)\geq0,\ldots,g_m(x)\geq0\}\) and let \(T(g)\) be the preordering generated by \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\). For \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\), \(f>0\) on \(K\) if and only if there exist \(p,q\in T(g)\) such that \(pf=1+q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial is strictly positive on a basic closed set exactly when multiplication by a preordering element yields one plus another preordering element.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f>0\text{ on }K\iff \exists p,q\in T(g):\ pf=1+q\).

notation.meaning: preordering generated by the constraint polynomials

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Krivine–Stengle Denominator Certificate
Constrained Denominator Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rational positivity certificates over a basic closed, possibly noncompact semialgebraic set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\geq0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), and let \(T(g)\) denote the preordering generated by \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\). For \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\), a constrained-denominator certificate consists of \(q\in\mathbb R[x]\) and \(t\in T(g)\) satisfying
\[
q^2f=t,
\qquad q(x)\neq0\quad\text{for every }x\in K.
\]
Because every element of \(T(g)\) is nonnegative on \(K\) and the denominator has no feasible zeros, this finite identity certifies \(f\geq0\) on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A denominator nonvanishing on the feasible set transforms the target polynomial into the constraint preordering, thereby certifying feasible nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)\geq0\) for every \(x\in K\).

notation.meaning: Preordering generated by the constraint polynomials.
Polynomial denominator nonvanishing on the feasible set.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed identity is a sound sufficient certificate and certificate is the correct content kind. No source supports this particular constrained-denominator formulation or its nonvanishing requirement.

children.title: Projective Infinity Geometry
children.top_down_role: Geometric conditions making affine behavior at infinity compatible with homogenized or projective certificate models.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomials with only isolated singularities at infinity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projective definition for a real polynomial, using its two highest homogeneous components and complex projective points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]\) have degree \(d\) and decomposition \(f=\sum_{i=0}^d f^i\), where each \(f^i\) is zero or homogeneous of degree \(i\). The polynomial \(f\) has only isolated singularities at infinity if it is constant, or, when it is nonconstant, there are only finitely many \(\mathbf z\in\mathbb P^{n-1}(\mathbb C)\) such that \(\partial f^d/\partial x_1(\mathbf z)=\cdots=\partial f^d/\partial x_n(\mathbf z)=f^{d-1}(\mathbf z)=0\). Moreover, when \(n=2\), every polynomial has only isolated singularities at infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial has only isolated singularities at infinity if it is constant or only finitely many complex projective points simultaneously annihilate all derivatives of its leading homogeneous component and its next-highest homogeneous component. Every polynomial in two variables has this property.
assumptions_latex: f^i\text{ is zero or homogeneous of degree }i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ has only isolated singularities at infinity}\iff f\text{ is constant or }\#\{\mathbf z\in\mathbb P^{n-1}(\mathbb C):\nabla f^d(\mathbf z)=0,\ f^{d-1}(\mathbf z)=0\}<\infty;\qquad n=2\Rightarrow\text{every }f\text{ has this property}

children.title: Homogenized Feasible Geometry
children.top_down_role: Projective closure of affine polynomial optimization models.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compactness of the Normalized Homogenized Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topological compactness supplied by hemisphere normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finitely many polynomial equality and nonstrict inequality constraints, the normalized homogenized set \(K^h\) is a closed subset of the unit sphere intersected with \(\{x_0\geq0\}\). Consequently \(K^h\) is compact, whether or not it equals the closure of its positive chart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hemisphere normalization makes the constructed homogenized feasible set compact independently of closedness at infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(K^h\) is defined by finitely many polynomial equalities and nonstrict inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K^h\text{ is compact}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Compactness of the Normalized Homogenized Model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint system induced on the homogenizing hyperplane.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write \(g_i^{\mathrm{top}}\) and \(h_j^{\mathrm{top}}\) for the highest-degree homogeneous parts of the affine constraints. Every \((0,y)\in K^h\) satisfies \(\|y\|=1\), \(g_i^{\mathrm{top}}(y)\geq0\), and \(h_j^{\mathrm{top}}(y)=0\). Thus the constructed boundary is determined by leading forms, although it need not equal the actual affine escape directions unless closedness at infinity holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the homogenizing boundary, leading constraint forms determine the candidate directions at infinity.
assumptions_latex: Each constraint is homogenized to its own degree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|y\|=1,\quad g_i^{\mathrm{top}}(y)\geq0,\quad h_j^{\mathrm{top}}(y)=0\).

notation.meaning: Leading homogeneous part of inequality generator g_i.
Leading homogeneous part of equality generator h_j.

knowledge_statements.title: Leading-Form Boundary Constraints

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence between affine feasible points and the positive chart under the stipulated normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(a^h(x_0,y)=x_0^{\deg a}a(y/x_0)\), every \(x\in K\) maps to \(\Phi(x)=(1,x)/\sqrt{1+\|x\|^2}\in K^h\cap\{x_0>0\}\). Conversely, every \((x_0,y)\in K^h\) with \(x_0>0\) satisfies \(y/x_0\in K\) and equals \(\Phi(y/x_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized affine lifting bijects the original feasible set with the positive homogenizing-coordinate chart.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is defined by the constraints homogenized in \(K^h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi:K\xrightarrow{\sim}K^h\cap\{x_0>0\}.\)

notation.meaning: Normalized homogeneous lift of an affine point.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Chart Correspondence
Homogenized Feasible Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spherical projective compactification of an affine basic semialgebraic feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\geq0,\ h_j(x)=0\}\). For a polynomial \(a\) of degree \(d_a\), define \(a^h(x_0,y):=x_0^{d_a}a(y/x_0)\). Its homogenized feasible geometry is
\[
K^h:=\{(x_0,y):x_0\geq0,\ x_0^2+\|y\|^2=1,\ g_i^h(x_0,y)\geq0,\ h_j^h(x_0,y)=0\}.
\]
Affine points embed as \(x\mapsto(1,x)/\sqrt{1+\|x\|^2}\); the slice \(K^h\cap\{x_0=0\}\) is the constructed projective boundary at infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenized constraints on a unit hemisphere compactify the affine feasible set and introduce a boundary slice representing candidate directions at infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is described by finitely many polynomial inequalities and equalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K^h\) is the normalized homogenized feasible set, with boundary \(K^h_\infty:=K^h\cap\{x_0=0\}\).

notation.meaning: Homogenization of polynomial a to its own degree.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized constraint homogenization is coherent, but it may exceed the actual projective closure and depends on a specific convention. An authoritative locator is required.

children.title: Closedness at Infinity
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between affine feasible points and the boundary introduced by homogenization.

knowledge_statements.title: Closedness at Infinity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact agreement between the homogenized model and the closure of its affine chart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K^h\) be the normalized homogenized feasible set and define its positive chart by \(K^h_+:=K^h\cap\{x_0>0\}\). The affine model is closed at infinity when
\[
K^h=\overline{K^h_+}.
\]
Equivalently, every \((0,y)\in K^h\) is the limit of normalized lifts of feasible affine points. Under this condition the equations and inequalities introduced by homogenization create no boundary point disconnected from the affine feasible geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every homogenized boundary point must be approachable by normalized affine feasible points; otherwise homogenization has introduced extra geometry at infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(K^h\) is the normalized homogenization of an affine polynomial feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K^h=\overline{K^h\cap\{x_0>0\}}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The closure equality precisely expresses the stated local notion and condition is the correct content kind, but the record has no citation.

children.title: Optimality at Infinity
children.top_down_role: Projective-boundary loci competing with affine global minimizers.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective values achievable along feasible sequences escaping every compact set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be unbounded and \(f:K\to\mathbb R\). Define
\[
f_\infty:=\lim_{R\to\infty}\inf\{f(x):x\in K,\ \|x\|\ge R\}\in\mathbb R\cup\{\pm\infty\}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
f_\infty=\inf_{\substack{x_k\in K\\\|x_k\|\to\infty}}\liminf_{k\to\infty}f(x_k).
\]
For \(f^*:=\inf_K f\), equality \(f_\infty=f^*\) means that infinity competes at the global infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The asymptotic infimum is the best limiting objective value along escaping feasible sequences; infinity competes with affine minimization when this value equals the global infimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_\infty=\inf_{\substack{x_k\in K\\\|x_k\|\to\infty}}\liminf_{k\to\infty}f(x_k).

notation.meaning: Asymptotic infimum along escaping feasible sequences.
Infimum over the affine feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Infimum at Infinity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Separation from Infinity Implies Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact localization when escaping sequences have values strictly above the affine infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed, let \(f:K\to\mathbb R\) be continuous and bounded below, and set \(f^*=\inf_K f\). If \(f^*<f_\infty\), then every sublevel set
\[
\{x\in K:f(x)\le\alpha\},\qquad f^*<\alpha<f_\infty,
\]
is nonempty and compact. Consequently, \(f\) attains \(f^*\) on \(K\). Equality \(f^*=f_\infty\) does not by itself imply either attainment or nonattainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict gap between the affine infimum and the best value at infinity produces a compact sublevel containing a minimizer; equality is inconclusive.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuous and bounded below on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}f(x)\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Separation from Infinity Implies Attainment
Optimality at Infinity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary vanishing condition relevant to lower-bound certificates for polynomial optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) have degree \(d\), let \(f^h\) be its degree-\(d\) homogenization, and let \(K^h_\infty\) be the feasible boundary at infinity. A point \((0,y)\in K^h_\infty\) is an optimality candidate at infinity when
\[
f^h(0,y)=f_d(y)=0,
\]
where \(f_d\) is the leading homogeneous part of \(f\). Indeed, for every affine lower bound \(\gamma\), the homogenized gap \(f^h-\gamma x_0^d\) restricts on \(x_0=0\) to \(f_d\); hence its boundary zeros persist independently of \(\gamma\) and may obstruct strict projective positivity certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible direction at infinity where the objective’s leading form vanishes remains a zero of every homogenized affine lower-bound gap.
assumptions_latex: \(K^h_\infty\) is the boundary of the homogenized feasible model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((0,y)\in K^h_\infty\) and \(f_d(y)=0\) imply \((f^h-\gamma x_0^d)(0,y)=0\) for every \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\).

notation.meaning: Leading homogeneous part of the objective.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The boundary identity is algebraically correct, but vanishing of the leading form alone is only a certificate-obstruction candidate, not a generally sufficient notion of optimality at infinity. A source must establish the intended version.

children.title: Spurious Projective Components
children.top_down_role: Homogenized components that distort the intended affine certificate problem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Raw Homogenization Can Create a Spurious Point at Infinity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A generator-wise homogenization strictly larger than the projective closure of its affine solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In affine coordinates \((x,y)\), consider
\[
x(x-1)=0,\qquad xy-1=0.
\]
The real affine solution set is \(\{(1,1)\}\). Homogenizing the displayed generators to degree two using \(z\) gives
\[
x(x-z)=0,\qquad xy-z^2=0.
\]
The resulting real projective variety contains \([0:1:0]\), although this point is not in the projective closure of the affine singleton. It is therefore a spurious point of the generator-defined homogenization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenizing a selected generating system can introduce a projective point at infinity not approached by any affine feasible point.
assumptions_latex: The displayed generators are homogenized individually to degree two.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: [0:1:0]\in V_{\mathbb R}(x(x-z),xy-z^2)\setminus\overline{\{[1:1:1]\}}.
knowledge_statements.title: Raw Homogenization Can Create a Spurious Point at Infinity
Spurious Projective Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary components satisfying homogenized constraints but absent from the affine feasible closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K^h\) be the normalized set defined by the homogenized constraints and let \(K^h_+:=K^h\cap\{x_0>0\}\). The spurious projective locus is
\[
S_\infty:=K^h\setminus\overline{K^h_+}.
\]
Any connected component or irreducible semialgebraic component contained in \(S_\infty\) satisfies the formal boundary constraints but is not approached by normalized affine feasible points. If \(S_\infty\neq\varnothing\), projective positivity or optimality conditions imposed on all of \(K^h\) may be strictly stronger than the intended affine conditions on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spurious components satisfy homogenized constraints at infinity but cannot be approached from the affine feasible set, potentially strengthening certificates incorrectly.
assumptions_latex: \(K^h\) is the normalized constraint-defined homogenization of an affine feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_\infty\neq\varnothing\) implies that the homogenized model is not closed at infinity and contains non-affine-limit components.

notation.meaning: Positive homogenizing-coordinate chart of the feasible model.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The locus correctly captures homogenized points outside the affine-chart closure and failure_boundary fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the terminology and formulation.

children.title: Structured Noncompact Extensions
children.top_down_role: Special unbounded geometries inheriting positivity or moment properties from additional structure.

children.title: Cylindrical Extension Regimes
children.top_down_role: Noncompact sets extending an Archimedean base by additional unbounded coordinates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Fiber Coercivity Localizes a Cylinder
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment on a compact-base cylinder under uniform growth in its free coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and compact and let \(f\in\mathbb R[x,y]\), where \(y\in\mathbb R^q\). Suppose
\[
\lim_{R\to\infty}\inf_{\substack{x\in K\\\|y\|\ge R}}f(x,y)=+\infty.
\]
Then every sublevel set of \(f\) in \(K\times\mathbb R^q\) is compact. Consequently, \(f\) attains its global minimum on the cylinder.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform coercivity in the unrestricted coordinates restores compact sublevels and attainment on a compact-base cylinder.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) tends uniformly to positive infinity as the free coordinate escapes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in K\times\mathbb R^q}f(x,y)\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Fiber Coercivity Localizes a Cylinder

assumptions_latex: \(g_i\in\mathbb{R}[x]\) and \(K=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_i(x)\ge 0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) is nonempty and compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C=K\times\mathbb{R}^q\) is noncompact, and Archimedeanity in the base variables does not bound its unrestricted coordinates.

notation.meaning: nonempty compact basic closed base set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic closed cylinders whose nonempty bounded base and free coordinates require different certificate assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb{R}[x]\), let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_i(x)\ge 0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), and assume that \(K\) is nonempty and compact. For \(q\ge 1\), the associated cylindrical extension is
\[
C=K\times\mathbb{R}^q=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+q}:g_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}.
\]
It is noncompact: boundedness is imposed only in the base variables \(x\), while the coordinates \(y\) are unrestricted. Consequently, Archimedeanity of the quadratic module generated by \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\) in \(\mathbb{R}[x]\) does not make the module generated by the same polynomials in \(\mathbb{R}[x,y]\) Archimedean.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cylindrical regime is a nonempty compact basic closed base multiplied by one or more unrestricted Euclidean coordinates; compactness of the base does not bound the extended set.
knowledge_statements.title: Cylindrical Extension Regimes

children.top_down_role: Low-dimensional unbounded geometries with specialized positivity representations.

children.title: Strip Geometry
children.top_down_role: Certificate assumptions specialized to feasible sets confined between parallel boundaries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict positivity representation on a closed planar strip.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a<b\) and let \(f\in\mathbb R[x,t]\) satisfy
\[
f(x,t)>0\qquad\text{for all }(x,t)\in[a,b]\times\mathbb R.
\]
Then there exist sums of squares \(\sigma_0,\sigma_1\in\mathbb R[x,t]\) such that
\[
f=\sigma_0+(x-a)(b-x)\sigma_1.
\]
Thus every polynomial strictly positive on the planar strip belongs to the quadratic module generated by \((x-a)(b-x)\), although the strip is noncompact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every polynomial strictly positive on a planar strip is an SOS plus the strip-defining quadratic times an SOS.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in\mathbb R[x,t]\) is strictly positive on \([a,b]\times\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\in\Sigma[x,t]+(x-a)(b-x)\Sigma[x,t].

notation.meaning: Cone of sums of squares in the strip coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Marshall Strip Positivstellensatz
Strip Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed polynomial strips with one bounded and one two-sided unbounded coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For real numbers \(a<b\), the closed strip is
\[
S=[a,b]\times\mathbb{R}=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^2:x-a\ge0,\ b-x\ge0\}.
\]
More generally, a one-direction strip over a compact basic closed set \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is \(K\times\mathbb{R}\). Its recession directions are precisely \((0,s)\) with \(s\in\mathbb{R}\); hence its defining inequalities bound the base coordinate but impose neither an upper nor a lower bound on the free coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strip is a compact interval, or compact basic closed base, times a real line; only the line coordinate is unbounded in both directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=[a,b]\times\mathbb{R}\) has the two-sided recession directions \(\{(0,s):s\in\mathbb{R}\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The elementary strip formula is correct, but the generalized recession-direction assertion needs a cited convention applicable to potentially nonconvex compact basic closed bases. No source is supplied.

children.title: Half-Line Geometry
children.top_down_role: Certificate assumptions specialized to one-sided unbounded domains.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact univariate nonnegativity certificate on the nonnegative ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A polynomial \(p\in\mathbb R[t]\) is nonnegative on \([0,\infty)\) if and only if
\[
p(t)=\sigma_0(t)+t\sigma_1(t)
\]
for sums of squares \(\sigma_0,\sigma_1\in\mathbb R[t]\). If \(\deg p=2m\), one may take \(\deg\sigma_0\le2m\) and \(\deg\sigma_1\le2m-2\). If \(\deg p=2m+1\), one may take \(\deg\sigma_0\le2m\) and \(\deg\sigma_1\le2m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A univariate polynomial is nonnegative on the nonnegative half-line exactly when it is an SOS plus t times an SOS.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\ge0\text{ on }[0,\infty)\iff p=\sigma_0+t\sigma_1,\quad\sigma_0,\sigma_1\in\Sigma[t].

notation.meaning: Cone of sums of squares of real univariate polynomials.

knowledge_statements.title: Half-Line Sum-of-Squares Representation

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H=K\times[0,\infty)\) has boundary face \(K\times\{0\}\) and global recession directions \(\{(0,s):s\ge0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided cylindrical geometry represented by a nonnegative unbounded coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) be nonempty and compact. The half-line extension of \(K\) is
\[
H=K\times[0,\infty)=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+1}:g_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m,\ t\ge0\}.
\]
Its boundary face at the endpoint of the ray is \(K\times\{0\}\). Its global recession directions, meaning vectors \(v\) such that \(z+\lambda v\in H\) for every \(z\in H\) and every \(\lambda\ge0\), are precisely \(\{(0,s):s\ge0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A half-line regime is a nonempty compact base times the nonnegative ray, with a boundary face at zero and one recession direction toward positive infinity.
knowledge_statements.title: Half-Line Geometry

children.title: Endpoint Positivity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Positivity behavior near finite endpoints of half-line domains.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive Endpoint Data Do Not Ensure Half-Line Positivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint traces do not control the compactified interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
p(t)=t^2-3t+1,
\]
one has \(p(0)=1>0\) and positive leading coefficient \(1\), but
\[
p(3/2)=-5/4<0.
\]
Thus positivity at the finite endpoint and compactified infinity is not sufficient for positivity on the whole half-line.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic can be positive at zero and at compactified infinity while negative at an interior half-line point.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive Endpoint Data Do Not Ensure Half-Line Positivity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite and infinite half-line endpoints represented as boundary traces on a compact interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x,t)=\sum_{k=0}^d f_k(x)t^k\) have degree \(d\) in \(t\), and put \(u=t/(1+t)\). Then
\[
F(x,u):=(1-u)^d f\!\left(x,\frac{u}{1-u}\right)
=\sum_{k=0}^d f_k(x)u^k(1-u)^{d-k}
\]
is polynomial on \(K\times[0,1]\). For \(0\le u<1\), \(F\) has the same sign as \(f\), while
\[
F(x,0)=f_0(x),\qquad F(x,1)=f_d(x).
\]
Thus the constant and leading coefficients are the finite-endpoint and compactified-infinity traces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The substitution u=t/(1+t) compactifies the half-line and turns the constant and leading coefficients into its two endpoint traces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(x,0)=f_0(x)\quad\text{and}\quad F(x,1)=f_d(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Compactification of Half-Line Endpoints
Endpoint Positivity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A uniform endpoint-and-infinity condition for polynomials on compact-base half-line extensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be compact and let
\[
f(x,t)=\sum_{k=0}^{d}f_k(x)t^k,\qquad d\ge1,
\]
with \(f_d\) not identically zero. The uniform endpoint-positivity regime on \(K\times[0,\infty)\) is the condition that there exist \(\varepsilon_0,\varepsilon_\infty>0\) such that
\[
f_0(x)\ge\varepsilon_0\quad\text{and}\quad f_d(x)\ge\varepsilon_\infty\qquad(x\in K).
\]
The first inequality controls \(t=0\); the second prevents degeneration of the highest-degree growth along \(t\to+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Endpoint positivity requires a uniform positive constant term on the base and a uniformly positive leading coefficient governing growth along the half-line.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x,0)\) is uniformly positive and the degree-\(d\) growth in \(t\) is uniformly nondegenerate on \(K\).

notation.meaning: leading coefficient in the unbounded coordinate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated uniform coefficient inequalities form a coherent condition and the content kind fits the leaf, but no source establishes that this is a recognized endpoint-positivity regime or connects it to a certificate theorem.

children.title: Unbounded-Direction Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of specialized representations along noncompact directions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Leading-Term Obstructions Along an Unbounded Fiber
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fiberwise asymptotic conditions forcing an objective to be unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a feasible base point \(x_0\) and write
\[
f(x_0,t)=a_dt^d+\text{lower-degree terms},\qquad a_d\ne0.
\]
On a feasible half-line fiber \(t\ge0\), if \(a_d<0\), then \(f(x_0,t)\to-\infty\). On a feasible two-sided fiber \(t\in\mathbb R\), if \(d\) is odd, one of the limits as \(t\to\pm\infty\) is \(-\infty\); if \(d\) is even and \(a_d<0\), both limits are \(-\infty\). In each case the full optimization problem has infimum \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative leading coefficient on a half-line, or an odd-degree or negatively led polynomial on a two-sided fiber, certifies unboundedness below.
assumptions_latex: The fiber \(\{x_0\}\times[0,\infty)\) or \(\{x_0\}\times\mathbb R\) is feasible.
\(a_d\ne0\) is the leading coefficient of the restricted polynomial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf f=-\infty\text{ on the feasible set in each stated leading-term case}.

notation.meaning: Leading coefficient along the unbounded coordinate at the fixed base point.

knowledge_statements.title: Leading-Term Obstructions Along an Unbounded Fiber
Unbounded-Direction Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict positivity can fail to provide a uniform margin when leading growth degenerates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On \(H=[0,1]\times[0,\infty)\), consider
\[
f(x,t)=(xt-1)^2+x^2.
\]
For every \((x,t)\in H\), one has \(f(x,t)>0\): at \(x=0\), \(f(0,t)=1\), while for \(x>0\) the two squares cannot vanish simultaneously. Nevertheless,
\[
\inf_{(x,t)\in H}f(x,t)=0,
\]
because \(f(x,1/x)=x^2\to0\) as \(x\downarrow0\). The leading coefficient in \(t\) is \(x^2\), which vanishes at the base endpoint and permits minimizing sequences to escape to infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This positive polynomial has infimum zero along an escaping sequence because its leading coefficient vanishes at a base endpoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f>0\) on \(H\), but \(\inf_H f=0\) and the infimum is not attained.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is mathematically correct and its content kind matches the failure-boundary leaf, but it has neither a citation nor an explicit permitted standard-field rationale in the evidence registry.

children.title: Convex Noncompact Regimes
children.top_down_role: Convex polynomial problems where saddle-point or curvature structure replaces standard compactness.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Noncompact Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and first-order global optimality for differentiable convex polynomials on closed convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(f\in\mathbb{R}[x]\) be convex. If some sublevel set \(\{x\in C:f(x)\le\alpha\}\) is nonempty and compact, then \(f\) attains its minimum on \(C\). Moreover, a point \(x^\star\in C\) is a global minimizer if and only if
\[
\langle\nabla f(x^\star),x-x^\star\rangle\ge0\qquad\text{for every }x\in C.
\]
Thus compactness of the whole feasible set is unnecessary when bounded sublevel geometry and convex first-order structure are available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex polynomial on a closed convex noncompact set attains its minimum when it has a compact nonempty sublevel set; a variational inequality characterizes global minimizers.
assumptions_latex: A nonempty compact sublevel set of \(f\) over \(C\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\neq\varnothing\), and \(x^\star\) is optimal exactly when \(\langle\nabla f(x^\star),x-x^\star\rangle\ge0\) for all \(x\in C\).

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Convex Sets p. 33; 2.2 Convex and Concave Functions p. 35

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 Convex Sets p. 33; 2.2 Convex and Concave Functions p. 35

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of attainment without compact sublevel geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
C=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x\ge0,\ xy\ge1\}
 =\{(x,y):x>0,\ y\ge1/x\}.
\]
Then \(C\) is closed and convex. For the linear polynomial \(f(x,y)=y\),
\[
\inf_C f=0,
\]
but no feasible point has \(y=0\). Thus a convex polynomial problem on a closed convex noncompact set can have a finite unattained infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear objective over a closed convex semialgebraic epigraph has finite infimum zero but no minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_C f=0\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname*{argmin}_C f=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Convex Infimum Without Attainment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order and saddle-point optimality on a possibly noncompact convex polynomial feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
\min_x f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_i(x)\le0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\quad Ax=b,
\]
where \(f,g_i\) are differentiable convex polynomials. Assume feasibility and the existence of \(\bar x\) satisfying \(A\bar x=b\) and \(g_i(\bar x)<0\) for all \(i\). A feasible point \(x^\star\) is globally optimal if and only if there exist \(\lambda_i\ge0\) and \(\nu\) such that
\[
\nabla f(x^\star)+\sum_i\lambda_i\nabla g_i(x^\star)+A^T\nu=0,
\qquad \lambda_i g_i(x^\star)=0.
\]
These multipliers yield a Lagrangian saddle point and zero primal-dual gap; compactness is unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Slater's condition, KKT multipliers are necessary and sufficient for global optimality in a differentiable convex polynomial program on a possibly noncompact set.
assumptions_latex: The affine equalities and convex inequalities are feasible.
Slater strict feasibility holds relative to the affine equality set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\text{ is optimal}\iff\exists(\lambda,\nu)\text{ satisfying feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity}.
knowledge_statements.title: Slater-Regular Convex Polynomial KKT Certificate

children.title: Archimedeanity Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for recognizing or constructing algebraic boundedness witnesses.

children.title: Explicit Bounding Structure
children.top_down_role: Recognition of bounding information already present among the generators.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Bounding Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A ball polynomial inside the quadratic module explicitly certifies Archimedeanity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For generators \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\subset\mathbb{R}[x]\), define
\[
M(g)=\left\{\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i:\sigma_i\text{ are sums of squares}\right\}.
\]
An explicit Archimedean witness is a number \(R>0\) and an identity
\[
R^2-\|x\|_2^2=\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i.
\]
Because the right side belongs to \(M(g)\), the identity directly verifies the Archimedean condition. It also implies that every point satisfying \(g_i(x)\ge0\) lies in the ball \(\|x\|_2\le R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SOS identity placing a ball constraint in the quadratic module certifies both Archimedeanity and boundedness of the described feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(R>0\) and each \(\sigma_i\) is a sum-of-squares polynomial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R^2-\|x\|_2^2\in M(g)\), so \(M(g)\) is Archimedean and \(\{g_i\ge0\}\subseteq\{\|x\|_2\le R\}\).

notation.meaning: quadratic module generated by the inequalities

children.title: Conic Archimedeanity Search
children.top_down_role: Finite-dimensional searches for algebraic boundedness witnesses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completeness of degree enumeration as a one-sided semidecision procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M(g)=\bigcup_{d\ge d_0}M_d(g)\), where \(M_d(g)\) is the degree-\(2d\) truncation of the quadratic module generated by \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\). If \(M(g)\) is Archimedean in the ball-witness sense, then there exist \(\rho>0\) and a finite order \(d_*\) such that \(\rho-\|x\|_2^2\in M_{d_*}(g)\). Consequently, a search that solves the truncated SOS feasibility problems at unboundedly increasing orders eventually finds a witness whenever one exists. If \(M(g)\) is non-Archimedean, the search need not terminate, and infeasibility at any finite collection of orders is inconclusive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing-degree SOS feasibility eventually succeeds for every Archimedean module, but it is only a semidecision procedure: non-Archimedeanity need not be detected in finite time.
assumptions_latex: \(M_d(g)\) are nested degree truncations with \(\bigcup_d M_d(g)=M(g)\).
The search visits arbitrarily large truncation orders.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Archimedeanity implies finite-order detection; non-Archimedeanity need not imply finite termination.

notation.meaning: A finite order containing an existing ball-witness representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Eventual Detection by Increasing-Degree Search
Conic Archimedeanity Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A degree-truncated semidefinite feasibility search for a ball witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb{R}[x]\) and an order \(d\), introduce \(\rho\ge0\) and Gram-matrix representations of sum-of-squares polynomials \(\sigma_i\) satisfying \(\deg(\sigma_i g_i)\le2d\), with \(g_0=1\). Solve the semidefinite feasibility problem
\[
\rho-\|x\|_2^2=\sum_{i=0}^m\sigma_i(x)g_i(x).
\]
If feasible, output \((\rho,\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m)\) as an Archimedean witness. If infeasible, increase \(d\); infeasibility at a fixed order does not certify non-Archimedeanity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each degree, solve an SDP for an SOS ball identity; feasibility proves Archimedeanity, while finite-order infeasibility is inconclusive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility yields \(\rho-\|x\|_2^2\in M(g)\); fixed-order infeasibility yields no converse certificate.

notation.meaning: SOS multiplier represented by a positive semidefinite Gram matrix

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The degree-truncated SDP is a valid one-sided search procedure, and it correctly states that fixed-order infeasibility is inconclusive. Its algorithmic and SOS-representation claims lack an authoritative source.

children.title: Bounding-Generator Augmentation
children.top_down_role: Description repair when independent feasible-set bounds are available.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Box-bound augmentation when independently validated coordinate bounds are available.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), and suppose independently validated constants \(B_i>0\) satisfy \(|x_i|\le B_i\) for every \(x\in K\). Append \(b_i(x)=B_i^2-x_i^2\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\). Then the augmented feasible set equals \(K\), and its quadratic module is Archimedean because \[\sum_{i=1}^n b_i(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n B_i^2-\|x\|_2^2\] belongs to that module. If any asserted coordinate bound is invalid, the augmentation may remove feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verified coordinate bounds may be appended as redundant quadratic inequalities; their sum is a ball witness, so the augmented module is Archimedean.
assumptions_latex: For each \(i\), an independently validated bound \(|x_i|\le B_i\) holds throughout \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Appending \(B_i^2-x_i^2\ge0\) preserves \(K\) and makes the augmented quadratic module Archimedean.
knowledge_statements.title: Coordinatewise Bounding-Generator Augmentation
Bounding-Generator Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Add a known redundant ball inequality to repair a non-Archimedean polynomial description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(K=\{x:g_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) and an independently established bound \(\|x\|_2\le R\) for every \(x\in K\), append
\[
g_{m+1}(x)=R^2-\|x\|_2^2.
\]
Output the augmented description \(K'=\{x:g_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m+1\}\). The independent bound makes the new inequality redundant, so \(K'=K\). Since \(g_{m+1}\) itself belongs to the augmented quadratic module, that module is Archimedean. Without a valid external bound, the augmentation may improperly remove feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verified global radius permits adding a redundant ball generator, preserving the feasible set while making the resulting quadratic module Archimedean.
assumptions_latex: An independent valid bound \(\|x\|_2\le R\) holds on all of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K'=K\), and the quadratic module generated by \(g_1,\ldots,g_m,R^2-\|x\|_2^2\) is Archimedean.

notation.meaning: set defined by the augmented generators

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Given a valid independent radius, the augmentation preserves the feasible set and makes the augmented module Archimedean. The algorithm content kind fits, but the claim has no cited source and depends essentially on external validation of the bound.
